የተባበሩት መንግሥታት ድርጅት የኢንዱስትሪ ድርጅት (UNIDO) እ.ኤ.አ. በ2017 ይፋ ባደረገው ጥናታዊ ሪፖርት ውጤት መሠረት፣ በኢትዮጵያ ከወደብ ችግር ጋር ተያይዞ የወጪ ምርቶችን አጓጉዞ ወደ ሸማቾች ለማድረስ የሚወስደውን ጊዜ በሳምንታት ያህል እንዲዘገይ ያደርጋል፡፡ በተለይ እንደ አትክልት፣ ፍራፍሬ፣ ቡና፣ ወዘተ ያሉ በቀላሉ የሚበላሹ የግብርና ምርቶችን በሰዓቱ ለገበያ ማድረስ ስለማይቻል በወጪ ንግድ አፈጻጸም ላይ ከፍተኛ አሉታዊ ተፅዕኖ እያሳዳረ ያለ ችግር ነው፡፡ የዓለም አቀፍ የቡና ድርጅት (ICO) እና የኢትዮጵያ ብሔራዊ ባንክ (NBE) ያደረጓቸው ጥናቶች እንዳመላከቱት፣ በኢንዱስትሪ ፓርኮች በጨርቃ ጨርቅ ምርቶች ላይ የተሰማሩ አምራቾች ምርቶቻቸው ለዓለም አቀፍ ገበያ በታዘዙበት የጊዜ ሰሌዳ ማቅረብ ባለመቻላቸው፣ ለተለያዩ ቅጣቶች (በዋናነት የዋጋ ቅናሽ እንዲያደርጉ) ተዳርዋል፡፡ በዚህም በኢትዮጵያ በወጪ ንግድ የተሰማሩ ላኪዎችና አምራቾች አብዛኛውን ጊዜ እስከ 20 ቀናት በሚደርሰው መዘግየት ምክንያት በሚደርስባቸው የዋጋ ቅናሽ በአማካይ ከ20 እስከ 25 በመቶ የሚሆን የወጪ ንግድ ገቢያቸውን ያጣሉ፡፡
ብሩኪንግ ኢንስቲትዩሽን (Brookings Institution) የተባለ ተቋም እ.ኤ.አ. በ2021 ያደረገው ጥናት ውጤት እንደሚጠቁመው፣ ኢትዮጵያ በወደብ የሎጂስቲክስ መዘግየት ምክንያት በ2021 ከቡና ወጪ ንግድ ማግኘት የሚገባት የውጭ ምንዛሪ በ18 በመቶ ቀንሷል፡፡ የአሜሪካ ዓለም አቀፍ ተራድኦና ልማት ድርጅት (USAID) እ.ኤ.አ. በ2018 ባካሄደው ጥናት ላይ እንደተመለከተው፣ በኢትዮጵያ የቡና ላኪዎች ለትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ አማካይ ወጪ ከቡና ሽያጭ ከሚያገኙት ገቢ 28 በመቶ ይደርሳል፡፡ በዚህም ምክንያት የኢትዮጵያ ቡና በዓለም አቀፍ ገበያ ዋጋው ከፍ እንዲል በማድረግ ተወዳዳሪነቱን እንዲቀንስ እያደረገ ያለ ችግር ነው፡፡
የኢትዮጵያ ኢንቨስትመንት ኮሚሽ (EIC) እና ማኪንሲ (McKinsey & Co) የተባለው ዓለም አቀፍ አማካሪ ድርጅት እ.ኤ.አ. በ2020 በጋራ ያካሄዱት ጥናት ውጤት እንደሚያሳየው፣ በጨርቃ ጨርቅ ምርት ላይ የተሰማሩ አምራቾች በወደብ ችግር ምክንያት ምርቶቻቸውን በወቅቱ ለዓለም አቀፍ ገበያ ማቅረብ ስለሚቸግራቸው፣ ከደንበኞቻቸው የሚደርስባቸውን አመኔታና ቅጣት ለመቀነስ የአየር ትራንስፖርት ወይም የአውሮፕላን ካርጎ ለመጠቀም ይገደዳሉ፡፡ የአውርፕላን ካርጎ ከመርከብ ትራንስፖርት አንፃር ዋጋው በአራት እጥፍ የሚጨምር በመሆኑ ገቢያቸውንና ትርፋማነታቸውን በከፍተኛ ደረጃ እንዲቀንስ አድርጓል፡፡
ኢትዮጵያ ወደብ አልባ በመሆኗ ወደ አገር ውስጥ በምታስገባቸው ምርቶች ላይ ከፍተኛ የዋጋ ጭማሪ እንዲኖር አድርጓል፡፡ የተባበሩት መንግሥታት ድርጅት የንግድና ልማት ማዕከል (UNCTAD) እ.ኤ.አ. በ2020 ባወጣው የጥናት ሪፖርት እንደተጠቀሰው፣ ኢትዮጵያ የወደብ ተደራሽነት ችግር ምክንያት የትራንስፖትና ሎጂስቲክስ ወጪ ከገቢ ሸቀጦች ዋጋ ከ40 እስከ 50 በመቶ እንዲሆን ያደረገ ነው፡፡
በጥናቱ እንደተገለጸው በአንፃሩ ወደብ ያላቸው የአፍሪካ አገሮች የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ ወጪ ከገቢ ምርቶች ዋጋ ከ10 እስከ 20 በመቶ ብቻ ነው፡፡ በወደብ ችግር ምክንያት በሚገጥም የትራንስፖትና ሎጂስቲክስ ችግር የሚደርስ የኢኮኖሚ ኪሳራ ዙሪያ ጥናት ያደረጉ በርካታ ምሁራን እንደ ዓለም አቀፍ ምሳሌ የሚጠቅሱት የጂቡቲ ወደብ ኮሪደርን ወይም ኢትዮጵያን ነው፡፡ ኢትዮጵያ የወደብ ችግሩ የሚያሳድረውን ጫና ለመቀነስ የተለያዩ ዕርምጃዎችን ስትወስድ ቆይታለች፡፡ ከእነዚህም መካከል በጂቡቲ ወደብ ላይ ያላትን ጥገኝነት ለመቀነስ አማራጭ ወደቦችን መፈለግ አንዱ ነው፡፡ ሌላው ደግሞ የአገሪቱ የዓለም አቀፍ ንግድ ኮሪደር የሆነው የኢትዮ-ጅቡቲ መስመር የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ መሠረተ ልማቶች የማሸሻል ሥራ አንዱ ነው፡፡
ከእነዚህ ተጠቃሹ እ.ኤ.አ. በ2010 የኢትዮ-ጂቡቲ ምድር ባቡር አቅም የማሳደግ ፕሮጀክት ነው፡፡ ከቻይና መንግሥት በተገኘ 4.5 ቢሊዮን ዶላር ብድር የተከናወነው ይህ ፕሮጀክት ቀድሞ የነበረውን የባቡር መሠረተ ልማት በከፍተኛ ደረጃ በመቀየር፣ 752 ኪሎ ሜትር የሚረዝም የኤሌክትሪክ ኃይል የተገጠመለት የባቡር ሐዲድ ግንባታ እ.ኤ.አ .በ2016 ተጠናቆ ለአገልግሎት ክፍት ሆኗል፡፡ በውጤቱም የወጪና የገቢ ሸቀጥ ጭነቶችን ከመሀል አገር ወደ ጂቡቲ ወደብ ለማድረስ ወይም ለማስገባት ይፈጅ የነበረው ጊዜ በአማካይ ከ72 ሰዓታት ወደ 12 ሰዓታት፣ እንዲሁም የሎጂስቲክስ ወጪን በአማካይ ከ20 እስከ 30 በመቶ እንዲቀንስ አስችሏል፡፡ የኢትዮ-ጅቡቲ የባቡር ፕሮጀክት የሎጂስቲክስ ሥርዓቱ ቀልጣፋ እንዲሆን በማድረጉ ዓመታዊ ጥቅል ምርት ላይ የ0.5 በመቶ ጭማሪ እንዲያሳይ አስተዋጽኦ አድርጓል፡፡ የተባበሩት መንግሥታት ድርጅት የንግድና ልማት ማዕከል (UNCTAD) እ.ኤ.አ. በ2020 ‹‹Review of Maritime Transport›› በሚል ርዕስ ይፋ ያደረገው ጥናት እንደጠቆመው እንደ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ሩዋንዳና ዛምቢያ ያሉ ወደብ አልባ አገሮች ከወደብ ጋር ተያይዞ የሚገጥማቸው ችግር ቢፈታ ኢኮኖሚያቸው በአማካይ በሁለት በመቶ እንዲያድርግ ያደርጋል፡፡
ኢትዮጵያ ወደብ አልባ መሆኗ የውጭ ቀጥታ ኢንቨስትመንት እንዲቀንስ አድርጓል
ሮድሪጌ፣ ኖቴቡምና ፓሊስ የተባሉ ተመራማሪዎች እ.ኤ.አ. በ2020 ያሳተሙት የጥናት ውጤት እንደሚጠቁመው፣ የወደብ አገልግሎት ከንግድ ጋር ተያይዞ ያሉ ሌሎች የኢኮኖሚ እንቅስቃሴዎች ለምሳሌ የሎጂስቲክስ፣ የማኑፋክቸሪንግና የአገልግሎት ዘርፎች እንዲጠናከሩ ያደርጋል፡፡ የወደብ ከተሞች የኢንዱስትሪ መንደሮች መናኸሪያ ናቸው፡፡ ምክንያቱም በወደብ አቅራቢያ መሆናቸው ጥሬ ዕቃዎችን ከውጭ ለማስገባት ወይም ምርቶችን ወደ ውጭ ገበያ ለመላክ የሚያስፈልገውን የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ ወጪ በከፍተኛ ሁኔታ ስለሚቀንስ፣ በዚህም ምርትን አምርቶ ወደ ገበያ ለማቅረብ ወጪን ስለሚቀንስ ነው፡፡ በዚህም አምራች ኢንዱስትሪዎች ምርቶቻቸው በዓለም አቀፍ ገበያ ተወዳዳሪ ስለሚሆን በማኑፋክቸሪንግ ዘርፍ የውጭ ቀጥታ ኢንቨስትመንት እንዲያድግ ትልቅ አስተዋጽኦ ያደርጋል፡፡
‹The Cost of Being Landlocked› በሚል ርዕስ አርዪስ፣ ራባላንድና ማርቲዩ የተባሉ ተመራማሪዎች እ.ኤ.አ. በ2010 ባሳተሙት የጥናት ሥራቸው እንደተመለከተው፣ ወደብ አልባ አገሮች የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ ወጪቸው ከፍተኛ በመሆኑ፣ በዚህም የማምረቻ ወጪያቸው ከፍ ስለሚል ሸቀጦቻቸው በዓለማቀፍ ገበያ ውድ ይሆናሉ፡፡ ሊሞና ቪነብልስ የተባሉ ተመራማሪዎች በጥናታቸው እንዳረጋገጡት ወደብ አልባ አገሮች ወደብ ካላቸው ጋር ሲነፃፀሩ የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ ወጪያቸው በ50 በመቶ ከፍ ይላል፡፡ በተጨማሪም ወደብ አልባ አገሮች ምርቶቻቸውን ዓለም አቀፍ ሸማቾች (ገዥዎች) በሚፈልጉት ወቅት ለማቅረብ ይቸገራሉ፡፡ ይህም የንግድ ተወዳዳሪነታቸውን (ተመራጭነታቸውን) በከፍተኛ ደረጃ ይቀንሰዋል፡፡
ኢትዮጵያ ወደብ አልባ መሆኗ ኢኮኖሚዋና ብሔራዊ ደኅንነቷ አደጋ ውስጥ እንዲወድቅ አድርጓል
በወደብ ችግር ምክንያት በሚገጥም የትራንስፖርትና ሎጂስቲክስ ችግር የሚደርስ የኢኮኖሚ ኪሳራ ላይ ጥናት ያደረጉ በርካታ ምሁራን እንደ ዓለም አቀፍ ምሳሌ የሚጠቅሱት የጂቡቲ ወደብ ኮሪደርን ወይም ኢትዮጵያን ነው፡፡ የተባበሩት መንግሥታት ድርጅት የንግድና ልማት ኮንፍራንስ እ.ኤ.አ. በ2020 ባወጣው ሪፖርት እንዳሳሰበው፣ ኢትዮጵያ በጂቡቲ ወደብ ላይ ጥገኛ መሆኗ የአገሪቱ ኢኮኖሚ ላይ ስትራቴጂያዊ ሥጋት ውስጥ እንዲወድቅ ያደረገ በመሆኑ ለችግሩ አፋጣኝ መፍትሔ ያስፈልጋል ብሏል፡፡ በአጠቃላይ የኢትዮጵያ የባህር በር ጥያቄን የመፍታት ጉዳይ ከኢኮኖሚው አልፎ የአገሪቱን ብሔራዊ ደኅንነት ከአደጋ የመታደግ ፋይዳ ያለው ነው፡፡ በመሆኑም ሁሉም የአፍሪካ ቀንድ አገሮች የኢትዮጵያን የባህር በር ጥያቄ በዚህ አግባብ ተረድተው አገሪቱ በሰላማዊ መንገድ ወደብ የምታገኝበትን መፍትሔዎች ማፈላለግ ለነገ የማይሉት የቤት ሥራ ነው፡፡
ከአዘጋጁ፡- ጸሐፊው በኬንያ ናይሮቢ ከተማ በሚገኘው የአፍሪካ ኢኮኖሚክ ሪሰርች ኮንሶርቲየም (AERC) የምርምር ፌሎው፣ በተጨማሪም በናይጄሪያ አንጋፋ የትምህርት ተቋም በሆነው ዩኒቨርሲቲ ኦፍ ኢባዳን የሦስተኛ ዓመት የፒኤችዲ (በኢነርጂ ኢኮኖሚክስ) ተመራማሪ፣ በተለያዩ ርዕሰ ጉዳዮች ላይ ያተኮሩ አሥር መጻሕፍትን የጻፉ፣ በቅርቡ ደግሞ ‹የኢትዮጵያ የባህር በር ጥያቄ› እንዲሁም ‹የአሰብ ጉዳይና የኢትዮ ኤርትራ ግንኙነት› የተሰኙ ሁለት መመጻሕፍት ያሳተሙ ሲሆን፣ ጽሑፉ የእሳቸውን አመለካከት ብቻ የሚያንፀባርቅ መሆኑን እየገለጽን በኢሜይል አድራሻቸው [email protected] ማግኘት ይቻላል፡፡
a1166.en:
How is Ethiopia's sea-access question viewed from a geo-economics perspective?

By Habtamu Girma Demissie

Introduction

Until Eritrea gained its independence in 1983 (Ethiopian calendar), Ethiopia conducted 97 percent of its export and import trade through the port of Assab. After Eritrea's independence, landlocked Ethiopia continued to use Assab on a lease basis. However, following the outbreak of the Ethio-Eritrean war in 1990 (Ethiopian calendar), the port of Assab was closed. As a result, the country's national security was put at risk. At the time, the alternative Ethiopia had was to use the port of Djibouti. But because the port of Djibouti at that time had the capacity to handle only about one quarter of Ethiopia's port requirements, Ethiopia faced a major logistics problem and, beyond that, a national security problem. In the years after the turn of the European millennium, the port of Djibouti was expanded on the basis of Ethiopia's needs. From that time onward, Ethiopia has conducted between 90 and 97 percent of its trade through the port of Djibouti.

What is geo-economics?

Geo-economics refers to the activity a country undertakes, using its geographical position, to protect its geopolitical interests so that its economic security, and by extension its national security, is not put in danger. Geo-economics differs from conventional economics teaching (which sets out a formula for allocating scarce resources in a cost-saving manner in order to reach mutual benefit) in that its purpose is to enable a country to use geographic conditions to achieve its economic or geopolitical objectives in order to safeguard its national interests.

Ethiopia's sea-access question, viewed from a geo-economics perspective, can be seen from two sides. On the one hand, because the country is landlocked, it has faced difficult conditions both in bringing in from the international market the consumption or production inputs that are essential for basic economic activity and in delivering the country's products to the international market. On the other hand, the desires and concrete actions of neighbouring countries that have sea access to use the port as an instrument to exert influence over Ethiopia have been an observed problem over the past three decades since Ethiopia became landlocked.

Studies show that the benefit of efficient port services in accelerating economic growth can be seen in three parts. The first is that a port raises a country's competitiveness in the international market and thereby increases trade's contribution to economic growth. The second way a port becomes decisive for a country's economy is through its critical role in increasing investment and in expanding infrastructure and industry. Third, we see the importance of the port in the maritime sector's contribution to economic growth.

Ethiopia's being landlocked has reduced its international trade competitiveness

A port is fundamental to a country's economy. Especially for countries like Ethiopia with a large population and a growing economy, a port is as essential as a blood vessel. Countries with ports, compared with countries without ports, can trade internationally directly, quickly, efficiently and at lower cost. By contrast, countries without ports become dependent on their port-owning neighbours along the international trade route. Port access and economic growth are deeply interlinked matters.

Port access raises a country's linkage with the international market by reducing transport and logistics costs. Especially for developing countries like Ethiopia, the port determines the level of bilateral trade relations with other countries. As shown in the study published by Coulibaly and Fontagne under the title 'South-South Trade', if landlocked African countries' port access were increased by ten percent, their annual export performance would grow on average by twenty percent.

Because of the logistics problem faced by landlocked African countries such as Ethiopia, the prices of export and import goods become high. A study carried out by the World Bank in 2014 shows that, compared with African countries that have ports, those without ports face logistics costs in international trade that are three times higher. Countries with a port problem suffer effects on their export trade because of the delays they face in passing through the customs procedures of the country from which they obtain port access. As the result of the study published by the researchers Djankov and Freund under the title 'Trading On Time' states, because of the trade delays that landlocked countries' products face in connection with customs services, their exports decline by one percent for each day of delay.

As the World Bank study result shows, Ethiopia, which is landlocked and which conducts 95 percent of its international trade through the port of Djibouti, sees its importers and exporters exposed to various additional costs because of the bureaucratic problems created by the customs procedures that the Djiboutian government changes from time to time. Because this logistics delay makes it difficult both to load cargo onto ships on time and to bring it from the port into the country, it has exposed the country to additional transport costs, warehouse rental and related expenses. For this reason, Ethiopia incurs an additional cost of between 1.5 and two billion dollars every year.

According to the results of the research report released by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in 2017, in Ethiopia the time taken to transport export products and deliver them to consumers is delayed by weeks in connection with the port problem. In particular, because perishable agricultural products such as vegetables, fruit, coffee and so on cannot be delivered to the market on time, this is a problem that is having a major negative effect on export performance. As studies conducted by the International Coffee Organization (ICO) and the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) have indicated, manufacturers engaged in textile production in the industrial parks have been subjected to various penalties (mainly being required to give price discounts) because they were unable to supply their products to the international market on the schedule that was ordered. As a result, exporters and producers engaged in export trade in Ethiopia lose on average between 20 and 25 percent of their export revenue because of the price discounts imposed on them owing to delays that often reach up to 20 days.

As the result of the study conducted in 2021 by the institution called the Brookings Institution indicates, because of port logistics delays the foreign exchange Ethiopia should have earned from coffee exports in 2021 fell by 18 percent. As shown in the study carried out in 2018 by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the average transport and logistics cost for coffee exporters in Ethiopia amounts to 28 percent of the income they earn from coffee sales. For this reason, it is a problem that is raising the price of Ethiopian coffee on the international market and thereby reducing its competitiveness.

As the result of the study jointly conducted in 2020 by the Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) and the international consultancy firm McKinsey & Co shows, because manufacturers engaged in textile production find it difficult to supply their products to the international market on time owing to the port problem, they are forced to use air transport or air cargo in order to reduce the loss of trust and the penalties imposed on them by their customers. Because air cargo is four times more expensive than sea transport, this has greatly reduced their revenue and their profitability.

Ethiopia's being landlocked has caused a significant price increase on the products it imports into the country. As stated in the study report issued by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) in 2020, Ethiopia's port access problem has caused transport and logistics costs to amount to between 40 and 50 percent of the price of imported goods.

As stated in the study, by contrast, for African countries that have ports transport and logistics costs are only between 10 and 20 percent of the price of imported goods. Many scholars who have conducted studies on the economic loss caused by transport and logistics problems arising from port constraints cite the Djibouti port corridor, or Ethiopia, as the global example. Ethiopia has been taking various measures to reduce the pressure exerted by the port problem. Among these, one is seeking alternative ports in order to reduce its dependence on the port of Djibouti. Another is the work of improving the transport and logistics infrastructure of the Ethio-Djibouti line, which is the country's international trade corridor.

Notable among these is the 2010 project to increase the capacity of the Ethio-Djibouti railway. This project, carried out with a 4.5 billion dollar loan obtained from the Chinese government, substantially transformed the previously existing railway infrastructure, and the construction of a 752-kilometre electrified railway line was completed and opened for service in 2016. As a result, the time it used to take to deliver export and import cargo from the interior of the country to the port of Djibouti, or to bring it in, fell on average from 72 hours to 12 hours, and it enabled logistics costs to fall by an average of 20 to 30 percent. Because the Ethio-Djibouti railway project made the logistics system efficient, it contributed to a 0.5 percent increase in annual gross output. As the study released by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) in 2020 under the title 'Review of Maritime Transport' indicated, if the port-related problems faced by landlocked countries such as Ethiopia, Rwanda and Zambia were resolved, it would enable their economies to grow by an average of two percent.

Ethiopia's being landlocked has reduced foreign direct investment

As the study result published in 2020 by the researchers Rodrigue, Notteboom and Pallis indicates, port services strengthen other trade-related economic activities, for example the logistics, manufacturing and service sectors. Port cities are the hub of industrial districts. This is because their proximity to the port greatly reduces the transport and logistics cost needed to import raw materials from abroad or to send products to foreign markets, and because it thereby reduces the cost of producing goods and bringing them to market. Because this makes manufacturing industries' products competitive on the international market, it makes a large contribution to the growth of foreign direct investment in the manufacturing sector.

As shown in the study work published in 2010 by the researchers Arvis, Raballand and Marteau under the title 'The Cost of Being Landlocked', because landlocked countries' transport and logistics costs are high, and because their production costs therefore rise, their goods become expensive on the international market. As the researchers Limao and Venables confirmed in their study, landlocked countries' transport and logistics costs are 50 percent higher compared with countries that have ports. In addition, landlocked countries find it difficult to supply their products at the time international consumers (buyers) want them. This greatly reduces their trade competitiveness (their preferability).

Ethiopia's being landlocked has put its economy and its national security in danger

Many scholars who have conducted studies on the economic loss caused by transport and logistics problems arising from port constraints cite the Djibouti port corridor, or Ethiopia, as the global example. As the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development warned in the report it issued in 2020, Ethiopia's dependence on the port of Djibouti has placed the country's economy under strategic risk and therefore an urgent solution to the problem is needed, it said. Overall, the matter of resolving Ethiopia's sea-access question has a value that goes beyond the economy to rescuing the country's national security from danger. Therefore, it is homework that cannot be left until tomorrow for all the countries of the Horn of Africa to understand Ethiopia's sea-access question in this light and to seek solutions by which the country can obtain a port by peaceful means.

From the editor: The writer is a research fellow at the African Economic Research Consortium (AERC) located in Nairobi, Kenya, and is also a third-year PhD researcher (in Energy Economics) at the University of Ibadan, a long-established educational institution in Nigeria. He has written ten books focused on various topics and has recently published two books titled 'Ethiopia's Sea Access Question' and 'The Assab Issue and Ethio-Eritrean Relations'. While we note that the article reflects only his own views, he can be reached at his email address.

a1192.t:
Trump aid freeze threatens completion of N$3.5m Unam project
The development reflects broader disruptions across various sectors in Namibia, triggered by recent shifts in American foreign funding policy under the administration of President Donald Trump.
The affected initiative, Strengthening University Systems to Improve Rural Education, was funded by the US State Department and the US Embassy in Windhoek. Valued at approximately N$3.5 million (US$200 000), the project was scheduled to run from October 2022 to October 2024; however, it was extended into 2025, during which the remaining work – valued at around N$90 000 – was to be completed.
According to Unam spokesperson Simon Namesho, another initiative, the Improving Rural Quality Education in Namibia and Iowa project, valued at approximately N$1.5 million, was also affected.
Steady partners
Namesho however highlighted that most of the university’s current projects are funded by partners in Canada, Japan, the European Union and Namibia itself.
“While some of our partners have been impacted by the US funding freeze, Unam’s current research is largely unaffected, as our major funding comes from other sources,” Namesho told Namibian Sun yesterday.
“For example, our Group for Research in Infectious Diseases is funded by the UK, the EU and the German government,” he explained.
Though Unam still maintains ties with US-based institutions like the National Institutes of Health (NIH), collaborations have become more difficult.
Namesho acknowledged that the cancelled US grant has disrupted plans for a postgraduate conference and affected some School of Education partnerships. Unam is also engaging in joint advocacy efforts with other African universities.
“We are in dialogue with African institutions and partners to coordinate responses to these funding challenges,” Namesho said.
Stable funding options
This is the latest among a series of reports on how Namibia has been affected by the American foreign aid freeze.
Namibian Sun recently reported on the Fulbright scholarships and several US-supported health, education and conservation programmes that have been suspended or delayed as Washington reassesses its foreign funding priorities.
Civil society organisations warn that the aid freeze jeopardises essential services for communities affected by HIV, youth unemployment and environmental degradation.
In response, Unam is accelerating efforts to diversify its research partnerships and reduce reliance on US donors. Namesho noted that the university is strengthening collaborations with European institutions and aligning itself with global research platforms such as the European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership (EDCTP).
“Namibia has formalised its association with the EDCTP, which enhances our eligibility for international health research funding,” he noted.
Unam is also working with the National Commission on Research, Science and Technology (NCRST) to unlock local and international funding channels. A dedicated research, innovation, and development fund is being finalised to provide more stable and self-reliant funding in the future.
Going forward
Meanwhile, increased support from the Namibian government, state-owned enterprises and the private sector has enabled the university to issue new calls for research proposals among academic staff.
While the university has yet to release an official statement on the broader implications of the US aid freeze, internal assessments are ongoing.
“We are currently assessing the full impact and will report once the process is complete,” Namesho confirmed. He added that Unam will be represented at the upcoming EDCTP annual general meeting in Kigali in June.
For now, most postgraduate students remain unaffected, as their funding comes from institutions such as GIZ, the EU and Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC).

a1327.t:
La Nation Bénin...
Face à la presse dans la matinée d’hier jeudi 18 décembre, l’Unité de Coordination de la formulation du 2è programme et du suivi des réformes de MCA-Bénin (UCF/ MCA-Bénin) a confirmé l’éligibilité du Bénin au 2è compact. Le contenu du programme pour les cinq années à venir ainsi que les avantages que le Bénin peut en tirer ont été présentés.
Le coordonateur national de l’UCF/MCA, Samuel Batcho, le directeur du Bénin au MCC, Christopher Broughton ainsi que le vice- président adjoint de MCC, Jonathan Bloom étaient face à la presse nationale dans la matinée d’hier jeudi 18 décembre.
 Visiblement content de voir le Bénin à nouveau élu au compact de MCC, le coordonnateur Samuel Batcho a d’abord dit la gratitude du gouvernement béninois au peuple américain ainsi qu'à son gouvernement. Il a ensuite salué l’entregent de l’ambassadeur des Etats-Unis près le Bénin dans l’aboutissement de ce dossier. Confirmant l’éligibilité du Bénin, le coordonnateur national de l’UCF/MCA a rappelé que c’est l’indicateur corruption qui était au rouge pour que le pays soit recalé. Il précise que c’est unanimement que la décision a été prise l’année dernière. Mais cette année, grâce aux progrès accomplis par chacun et surtout le Plan de lutte contre la corruption mis en place par le gouvernement, le pays a abouti à ce résultat positif qui donne le sourire à tous aujourd’hui.
 Pour Samuel Batcho, le Bénin n’a jamais passé auparavant plus de 11 indicateurs. Voilà que cette année il a fait la prouesse d’en passer 12. Puis Samuel Batcho de préciser que «si chacun met un peu du sien, s’il y a davantage d’efforts, le Bénin peut passer 13 voire 14 indicateurs».
 Les conférenciers se sont également appesantis sur le contenu du Programme dont ils disent qu’il sera exclusivement concentré sur le secteur énergétique au Bénin. Un secteur qu’il qualifie de stratégique pour son développement. «Si l’on peut fournir davantage d’électricité, cela peut libérer le moteur de croissance au Bénin», a laissé entendre le vice-président adjoint de MCC Jonathan Bloom qui souligne au passage la nécessité de monter un cadre attractif afin d’attirer les investissements de tout le monde. «Cela va exiger des efforts énormes de la part du MCC et des engagements de la part du gouvernement du Bénin», a dit le vice-président adjoint de MCC. Il ajoute espérer que cela aidera à pérenniser les rêves du peuple béninois.
 Autres explications apportées par le coordonnateur national de l’UCF/ MCA-Bénin, Samuel Batcho, c’est le montant des fonds. «Une enveloppe de base de 250 millions de dollars  américain», a-t-il souligné, avec la précision que le Ghana était à une enveloppe de base de 300 millions de dollars, mais avec la flexibilité des Américains, et le soutien de son secteur privé, l’enveloppe est allée à 500 millions de dollars américain. «Le Bénin aussi peut faire autant. Tout dépend de nous», a-t-il souligné.
 Pour sa part le vice-président adjoint de MCC, Jonathan Bloom, a invité chacun à progresser et aller au-delà du progrès réalisé par le Ghana. Il souhaite que le secteur privé saisisse l’occasion pour faire comme les Ghanéens.
 Pour ce qui est de la contrepartie du MCC dans la signature du compact avec le Bénin, Jonathan Bloom a précisé que c’est «juste pour qu’il y ait un monde plus juste, plus libre et plus prospère. C’est tout l’intérêt des USA», a-t-il conclu.
 La presse a posé beaucoup de questions relatives à ce qui sera fait concrètement, lorsqu’on parle de secteur de l’énergie au Bénin. Les conférenciers ont été très précis en assurant que des études de faisabilité seront faites. «Il y a aujourd’hui de nouvelles technologies pouvant aider à réduire la consommation électrique. Si le cadre institutionnel et stable est mis en place, cela peut attirer le secteur privé», a indiqué Jonathan Bloom
a1327.en:
Millennium Challenge Account Benin: Benin's eligibility for the MCC's 2nd compact explained to the press

La Nation Benin...

Facing the press yesterday, Thursday 18 December, in the morning, the Coordination Unit for the formulation of the 2nd programme and the monitoring of reforms of MCA-Benin (UCF/MCA-Benin) confirmed Benin's eligibility for the 2nd compact. The content of the programme for the coming five years, as well as the benefits Benin can draw from it, were presented.

The national coordinator of UCF/MCA, Samuel Batcho, the MCC's country director for Benin, Christopher Broughton, as well as the MCC Deputy Vice-President, Jonathan Bloom, faced the national press yesterday, Thursday 18 December, in the morning.

Visibly pleased to see Benin once again selected for the MCC compact, coordinator Samuel Batcho first expressed the Beninese government's gratitude to the American people and to their government. He then praised the resourcefulness of the United States Ambassador to Benin in bringing this matter to a successful conclusion. Confirming Benin's eligibility, the national coordinator of UCF/MCA recalled that it was the corruption indicator that was in the red, causing the country to be rejected. He specified that the decision was taken unanimously last year. But this year, thanks to the progress made by everyone and above all the anti-corruption plan put in place by the government, the country reached this positive result which brings a smile to everyone's face today.

For Samuel Batcho, Benin had never before passed more than 11 indicators. Now this year it has achieved the feat of passing 12. Samuel Batcho then specified that "if everyone does their bit, if there are more efforts, Benin can pass 13 or even 14 indicators."

The speakers also dwelt on the content of the Programme, which they say will be exclusively concentrated on the energy sector in Benin. A sector that they describe as strategic for its development. "If we can supply more electricity, that can unleash the engine of growth in Benin," suggested the MCC Deputy Vice-President Jonathan Bloom, who underlined in passing the need to build an attractive framework in order to attract investment from everyone. "This will require enormous efforts on the part of the MCC and commitments on the part of the government of Benin," said the MCC Deputy Vice-President. He added that he hoped this would help make the dreams of the Beninese people lasting.

Other explanations provided by the national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Benin, Samuel Batcho, concerned the amount of the funds. "A base envelope of 250 million US dollars," he emphasised, specifying that Ghana had a base envelope of 300 million dollars, but with the flexibility of the Americans and the support of its private sector, the envelope went up to 500 million US dollars. "Benin can do as much too. It all depends on us," he stressed.

For his part, the MCC Deputy Vice-President, Jonathan Bloom, invited everyone to make progress and to go beyond the progress achieved by Ghana. He hopes the private sector will seize the opportunity to do as the Ghanaians did.

As for the MCC's own stake in signing the compact with Benin, Jonathan Bloom specified that it is "just so that there is a fairer, freer and more prosperous world. That is the whole interest of the USA," he concluded.

The press asked many questions about what will concretely be done when one speaks of the energy sector in Benin. The speakers were very precise, assuring that feasibility studies will be carried out. "There are today new technologies that can help reduce electricity consumption. If a stable institutional framework is put in place, that can attract the private sector," indicated Jonathan Bloom.

a1456.t:
Key parts of Donald Trump's agenda have met resistance in court from federal judges, who have issued more than 70 rulings impeding the Republican president's efforts on a range of issues. These have included deportations, birthright citizenship, government spending, transgender service in the military, punitive directives against law firms and diversity, equity and inclusion programmes.
Here is a look at some of the more than 200 lawsuits filed by various plaintiffs to try to block Trump policies as he approaches the 100-day mark of his second term as president on Wednesday.
- January 20 - Inauguration as 47th President: Donald Trump is sworn in for a second, non-consecutive term, marking the beginning of a presidency characterised by rapid and controversial actions.
- January 21 - Executive Order on Immigration Enforcement: Trump signs an executive order intensifying immigration enforcement, including measures to end birthright citizenship and halt refugee admissions. These actions face immediate legal challenges.
- January 22 - Launch of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE): Led by Elon Musk, DOGE is established to streamline federal operations, claiming significant cost savings through cuts to various programs and agencies.
- January 25 - Implementation of Broad Tariffs: The administration imposes sweeping tariffs on imports from countries including China, Canada, and Mexico, aiming to boost domestic manufacturing but causing market instability.
IMMIGRATION CRACKDOWN
The US Supreme Court on 19 April temporarily barred Trump's administration from deporting Venezuelan men in immigration custody after their lawyers said they were at imminent risk of removal without the judicial review previously mandated by the justices. The administration has alleged that the Venezuelans are members of the Tren de Aragua criminal gang. Family members and lawyers for the migrants have disputed this.
Three federal judges subsequently criticised the administration's approach to immigration and temporarily halted new deportations in their judicial districts under the Alien Enemies Act, a 1798 law historically used only in wartime that Trump invoked as justification to remove certain people without hearings or other legal safeguards.
One of the judges, overseeing the case of a Salvadoran man living in Maryland who the administration has acknowledged was mistakenly deported to El Salvador, rebuked the government for trying to circumvent an order blocking additional deportations and misleading the court about its actions.
The two other judges voiced doubts about the legality of the administration's moves and temporarily barred it from removing additional detainees while they consider longer-lasting orders.
- Revocation of Biden-Era Orders (January 20, 2025): Rescinded 78 executive actions from the Biden administration, targeting policies on racial equity, climate change, gender identity, Covid-19 response, and immigration
- Birthright Citizenship (January 20, 2025): Seeks to end birthright citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants and some legal immigrants, challenging the 14th Amendment's interpretation.
- Mass Deportation and Border Emergency (January 20, 2025): Declared a national emergency at the US-Mexico border, reinstated the "Remain in Mexico" policy, barred asylum for new arrivals, and directed resources for mass deportations, including National Guard deployment.
- Tariffs (January 20, 2025): Imposed 25% tariffs on imports from Canada and Mexico starting 1 February, 2025, and 125% on Chinese imports, with "reciprocal" tariffs on over 75 countries. These are moving targets and are continually being amended or changed.
- DEI Elimination (January 20, 2025): Terminated all federal diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) programmes, offices, and positions, including in contracting and the military. Revoked decades-old orders like Lyndon Johnson's 1965 Equal Employment Opportunity order.
- Schedule F Reinstatement (January 20, 2025): Reinstated Schedule F, allowing reclassification of federal workers to ease firing of those deemed disloyal or politically unreliable.
- Transgender Restrictions (January 28, 2025): Banned gender-affirming care for minors under 19 using federal funds, barred transgender individuals from military service, and mandated recognition of only two sexes on federal documents.
- Deregulation (10-for-1 Rule) (February 1, 2025): Requires agencies to repeal ten regulations for every new one issued, building on Trump's first-term 2-for-1 rule. Mandates net regulatory costs for 2025 be significantly below zero.
- EO on January 6 Pardons (January 20, 2025): Pardoned nearly 1 600 individuals charged in the 6 January, 2021, Capitol riot and commuted sentences for 14 others, including Oath Keepers and Proud Boys members.
- TikTok Ban Delay (January 20, 2025): Extended ByteDance's deadline by 75 days (later extended again) to divest TikTok, pausing a federal ban after Trump's campaign videos gained traction on the platform.
Federal judges have issued at least 19 orders halting or curtailing for now the administration's ability to conduct mass deportations, defund refugee resettlement programs and restrict automatic birthright citizenship. Many of those rulings are under appeal.
The administration has won at least nine rulings in cases in which judges have declined to block the government from carrying out immigration raids in places of worship, mothballing an entry app for migrants and sending certain detainees to the U.S. naval base at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.
BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP
The Supreme Court has scheduled arguments on 15 May over Trump's bid to broadly enforce his executive order to restrict automatic birthright citizenship. The court did not immediately act on a request by Trump's administration to narrow the scope of three nationwide injunctions issued by judges blocking the policy.
READ: Mbeki: SA can still fix relations with the US
At issue is Trump's executive order that directed federal agencies to refuse to recognise the citizenship of children born in the United States who do not have at least one parent who is a US citizen or lawful permanent resident. Challengers argued that Trump's order violates a right enshrined in the U.S. Constitution's 14th Amendment that provides that anyone born in the United States is a citizen.
- February 5 - Executive Order on Car TariffsAn executive order introduces auto tariffs designed to encourage car manufacturers to complete production in the US, offering tax incentives for compliance. 
- February 10 - Mass Firings in Federal AgenciesThe administration initiates mass firings across federal agencies, targeting departments like education, justice, and USAid, leading to concerns about institutional independence. 
- February 15 - Revocation of Security ClearancesTrump revokes security clearances for several former officials and critics, raising alarms about the politicization of national security measures. 
- February 20 - Proposal to Restructure the Federal ReserveThe administration proposes significant changes to the Federal Reserve's structure, aiming to increase presidential control over monetary policy. 
GOVERNMENT SPENDING
Federal judges issued several rulings blocking Trump's administration from freezing trillions of dollars in grants, loans and other federal financial assistance. Elements of those orders remain in force despite administration efforts to walk back aspects of the policies.
Judges also separately blocked the administration's bid to claw back $20 billion in clean energy project grants, cut $11 billion in public health funds allocated to states and curtail funding for research at universities, medical centers and other institutions.
The administration has had better luck in its efforts to downsize and reshape the government through its Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, which has been spearheaded by billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk.
- March 1 - Launch of National Energy EmergencyTrump declares a national energy emergency, streamlining permitting processes for new oil drilling projects to increase domestic energy production. 
- March 5 - Proposal to Take Control of GazaIn a controversial move, Trump suggests U.S. control over Gaza, leading to international backlash and concerns over U.S. foreign policy direction. 
- March 10 - Implementation of Polygraph Tests for Federal EmployeesThe administration begins using polygraph tests to identify internal leaks, fostering a climate of fear within federal agencies. 
- March 15 - Proposal to Revoke Harvard's Tax-Exempt StatusAmid disputes over diversity policies, Trump proposes revoking Harvard University's tax-exempt status, though legal experts question the move's validity. 
- March 20 - Introduction of the Take It Down ActA bipartisan effort leads to the passage of the Take It Down Act, criminalizing non-consensual deepfake pornography, showcasing rare legislative cooperation. 
- March 25 - Announcement of Tax Reform PlansThe administration unveils plans to renew and expand tax cuts, including eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security payments. 
Multiple judges had ordered thousands of fired federal workers reinstated after finding their terminations were likely illegal, but appeals courts later paused those rulings. While some judges have barred DOGE from accessing federal databases, others have cleared it to scour agencies for possible savings.
TRANSGENDER RIGHTS
The administration asked the Supreme Court on April 24 to allow implementation of Trump's executive order banning transgender people from serving in the U.S. military, one of a series of Trump directives to curb transgender rights.
Trump's efforts targeting transgender rights have been slowed down in court, with judges issuing at least 14 orders blocking his military ban as well as his policies to house inmates in federal prisons corresponding to their birth sex and to restrict gender-transition care for people under age of 19.
DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION PROGRAMS
Four judges have temporarily blocked the administration from enforcing Trump's executive orders terminating diversity, equity and inclusion, or DEI, programs in the U.S. government and requiring recipients of federal grant funds to certify that they do not run DEI programs that violate anti-discrimination laws. Some conservatives have argued that such policies discriminate against white people and certain others.
- April 1 - Clash with Ukrainian President ZelenskyyTrump engages in a public dispute with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy over security assurances, straining U.S.-Ukraine relations. 
- April 10 - Proposal to Rename the Gulf of MexicoIn a move that garners widespread ridicule, Trump proposes renaming the Gulf of Mexico, reflecting his penchant for controversial statements. 
- April 20 - Reduction of International Travel to the USUnder Trump's leadership, international travel to the US declines further, attributed to stringent immigration policies and global perceptions. 
- April 29 - Approval Ratings and Public PerceptionAs the first 100 days conclude, Trump's approval rating stands at 39%, the lowest for any U.S. president at this point in office since modern polling began. 
EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING LAW FIRMS
Four judges have blocked for now Trump's punitive executive orders placing restrictions on four major law firms, deeming the directives as likely acts of retaliation for speech protected by the Constitution's First Amendment. Trump has targeted law firms that have represented clients who have challenged his policies in court, have employed lawyers who have been involved in prosecutorial investigations against Trump at the federal and state levels or represent people who previously have investigated him.
TARIFFS AND TRADE WAR
The administration faces at least seven lawsuits challenging Trump's sweeping tariffs against foreign trading partners. The suits accuse Trump of overstepping his authority under the Constitution by imposing the duties without congressional authorization. A judge in one of the cases denied a request for a temporary restraining order but still could impose a preliminary injunction blocking the tariffs. The other six cases have yet to be ruled on.

Le Conseil des ministres s’est réuni en session ordinaire, le mercredi 05 mars 2025, dans sa salle de délibérations au Palais de Koulouba, sous la présidence du général d’Armée Assimi Goita, président de la Transition, Chef de l’Etat.
- A l’entame de la session, Son Excellence le général d’Armée Assimi Goïta, Président de la Transition, Chef de l’Etat, a prié pour le repos de l’âme des disparus, présenté ses condoléances à leurs familles et formulé des vœux de prompt rétablissement aux blessés, suite aux drames survenus sur les sites d’orpaillage à Kokoyo, village de Danga, Cercle de Kangaba et à Bilalikoto, Cercle de Kenieba.
Le Chef de l’Etat a instruit le Gouvernement de renforcer les mesures pour éviter les drames humains et environnementaux dans notre pays.
Le président de la Transition, Chef de l’Etat a en outre instruit :
- l’abrogation des actes de nomination des responsables administratifs directement impliqués dans la survenance desdits incidents : Préfet, Sous-préfets, responsables des Forces de Sécurité (Police, Gendarmerie, Garde), des services locaux des Eaux et Forêts, services d’Assainissement et du Contrôle des Pollutions et des Nuisances, services subrégionaux de la Géologie et des Mines ;
- la relecture de certains textes juridiques pour, entre autres, mettre fin à la transaction dans le domaine environnemental, faciliter la récupération des équipements impliqués dans l’orpaillage, et leur affectation au patrimoine de l’Etat ;
- la suspension des permis d’exploitation des mines artisanales octroyé à des personnes de nationalité étrangère ;
- le lancement de la procédure de dissolution du Conseil communal de Dabia.
- Après examen des points inscrits à l’ordre du jour, le Conseil a :
– adopté des projets de texte ;
– et entendu des communications.
AU CHAPITRE DES MESURES LEGISLATIVES ET REGLEMENTAIRES
- Sur le rapport du ministre des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, le Conseil des Ministres a adopté des projets de texte relatifs à la ratification de la Convention d’appui budgétaire comprenant un prêt, signé à Bamako, le 26 février 2025, entre le Gouvernement de la République du Mali et le Fonds du Qatar pour le Développement.
Par cette convention, le Fonds du Qatar pour le Développement accorde au Gouvernement de la République du Mali un appui budgétaire d’un montant de 50 millions de dollars américains, soit 31 milliards 447 millions 500 mille F CFA environ, composé d’un prêt de 45 millions de dollars américains, soit 28 milliards 302 millions 750 mille F CFA environ.
Cet appui budgétaire permettra de soutenir les secteurs de l’aide humanitaire, du développement économique et de la santé, notamment la fourniture de denrées alimentaires, la réalisation de points d’eau, la réhabilitation et la construction d’infrastructures et le renforcement des moyens d’action de l’Administration et des Collectivités territoriales.
- Sur le rapport du ministre de l’Economie et des Finances, le Conseil des Ministres a adopté un projet d’ordonnance portant modification de la Loi n°06-067 du 29 décembre 2006, modifiée, portant Code général des Impôts.
Le Gouvernement a adopté la Loi n°2023-040 du 29 août 2023 portant Code minier en République du Mali pour tirer davantage profit de la rente minière.
Ce nouveau Code a introduit dans le dispositif minier une convention d’établissement pour la phase de recherche et une autre pour la phase d’exploitation, réduit la période de stabilité du régime fiscal, institué la redevance de la surproduction et la taxation des superprofits, augmenté la participation de l’Etat dans le capital de la société d’exploitation minière et supprimé les exonérations douanières en phase d’exploitation.
Il a également introduit la progressivité du taux de la taxe ad valorem et a permis la conclusion des protocoles d’accord entre le Gouvernement de la République du Mali et des sociétés minières.
Le projet d’ordonnance, adopté, modifie les article 240 et 425 en vue d’adapter le Code général des Impôts au nouveau Code minier.
Cette modification apporte les innovations ci-après :
- l’élargissement du champ d’application de l’Impôt Spécial sur Certains Produits aux marbres, aux lingots d’or et aux autres produits miniers ;
- la réduction du taux minimal de l’Impôt Spécial sur Certains Produits pour les marbres, les lingots d’or et les autres produits miniers de 5% à 3% ;
- l’extension du droit de timbre sur les intentions d’exportations à tous les produits miniers.
- Sur le rapport du ministre de la Santé et du Développement social, le Conseil des Ministres a adopté :
- un projet de décret fixant les délais et les modalités de conclusion des conventions entre la Caisse nationale d’Assurance Maladie et les prestataires de santé.
Le processus a abouti, après la mise en place du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Obligatoire et du Régime d’Assistance Médicale, à l’adoption de la Loi n°2018-074 du 31 décembre 2018 portant institution du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle.
La mise en œuvre de l’Assurance Maladie Universelle nécessite un système de conventionnement qui définit clairement les délais et les modalités de conclusion des conventions entre la Caisse nationale d’Assurance Maladie et les prestataires de santé.
Ainsi, le Décret n°10-577/P-RM du 26 octobre 2010 fixant les délais et les modalités de conclusion des conventions entre les prestataires de santé et la Caisse nationale d’Assurance Maladie a été adopté pour la mise en œuvre du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Obligatoire.
L’application de ce décret a révélé des insuffisances dans le cadre du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle qu’il convient de corriger pour étendre, notamment la prise en charge à toutes les catégories de travailleurs.
Le projet de décret, adopté, permettra d’organiser efficacement la prise en charge de tous les assurés et bénéficiaires du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle.
- un projet de décret portant approbation des conventions types de délégation de gestion dans le cadre du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle.
La Loi n°2018-074 du 31 décembre 2018 portant institution du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle prévoit la possibilité pour la Caisse nationale d’Assurance Maladie de déléguer, sous son contrôle, certaines missions à des organismes gestionnaires délégués et d’impliquer des sociétés commerciales dont l’expertise est avérée en matière de gestion du risque maladie.
Le projet de décret, adopté, permettra de mettre en place un mécanisme pour assurer le partage, selon les besoins, des fonctions entre la Caisse nationale d’Assurance Maladie et les organismes gestionnaires délégués.
- un projet de décret fixant les principes de la tarification préférentielle et les taux de couverture des prestations de soins de santé dans le cadre du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle.
Le Gouvernement a institué le Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle en vue de favoriser la mise en commun efficiente des ressources et l’achat stratégique en matière de soins de santé.
La fonctionnalité de l’assurance maladie universelle passe nécessairement par certains préalables parmi lesquels la précision des dispositions relatives à l’établissement de la tarification préférentielle des actes et des médicaments.
Le projet de décret, adopté, précise les principes de tarification et de remboursement des prestations offertes à tous les bénéficiaires du Régime d’Assurance Maladie Universelle.
AU CHAPITRE DES COMMUNICATIONS
- Le Ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, Garde des Sceaux a informé le Conseil des Ministres de la participation du Mali au « Segment de Haut Niveau » sur la situation des Droits de l’Homme, tenu du 24 au 26 février 2025, à Genève, en Suisse.
Le « Segment de Haut Niveau » sur la situation des Droits de l’Homme est un cadre permettant aux Chefs d’Etat ou de Gouvernement ou d’autres hauts dignitaires de faire l’état des lieux de la promotion et de la protection des Droits de l’Homme dans leurs pays respectifs.
Le Mali, à travers le ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, Garde des Sceaux, s’est adressé au Conseil des Droits de l’Homme pour porter des messages forts, notamment :
- réaffirmation de la détermination du Gouvernement du Mali à mettre en œuvre l’ensemble des recommandations acceptées lors de l’Examen Périodique Universel et des engagements pris lors de l’Evènement de haut niveau « Droits de l’Homme 75 » ;
- l’amélioration remarquable de la situation sécuritaire globale grâce aux efforts des Forces armées et de Sécurité et leurs partenaires stratégiques ;
- la mutualisation des moyens de défense par les Chefs d’Etat de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel, en vue de lutter efficacement contre le terrorisme ;
- l’appropriation de la résolution endogène des crises multidimensionnelles par l’élaboration en cours de la Charte nationale pour la paix et la réconciliation nationale ;
- la détermination du Gouvernement à lutter contre l’impunité sous toutes ses formes ;
- la réitération de l’appel adressé à la Communauté internationale en vue d’éviter la politisation et l’instrumentalisation des Droits de l’Homme ;
- la réaffirmation de la volonté du Gouvernement du Mali à poursuivre, dans le strict respect de sa souveraineté et des intérêts vitaux du Peuple malien, sa coopération avec tous les mécanismes de promotion et de protection des Droits de l’Homme.
En marge des travaux du « Segment de Haut Niveau », le ministre a eu une audience avec le Haut- Commissaire des Nations Unies aux Droits de l’Homme, sur les efforts et les progrès en matière de Droits de l’Homme au Mali, la reprise et le renforcement des relations de coopération entre le Mali et le Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies aux Droits de l’Homme.
- Le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique a informé le Conseil des ministres des conclusions de sa mission à Tombouctou du 25 au 27 février 2025.
Les objectifs de cette mission étaient, entre autres :
– de s’enquérir de l’état d’avancement de l’opérationnalisation de l’Université de Tombouctou aux fins d’identifier les actions et mesures à entreprendre ;
– d’échanger avec les autorités administratives, coutumières et de l’éducation à l’effet d’apporter des pistes de solution appropriées aux défis liés à l’opérationnalisation de l’Université de Tombouctou ;
– de visiter le site prévu pour la construction des infrastructures de l’Université.
Dans le cadre du démarrage effectif de l’Université de Tombouctou, le département a procédé à la nomination du Coordinateur chargé des activités d’opérationnalisation de l’université, à la rénovation de certains locaux administratifs et pédagogiques et à la tenue de la première session du Conseil d’Administration de l’Institut des Hautes Etudes et de Recherche Islamique Ahmed Baba de Tombouctou, une composante de ladite université.
A travers les différentes rencontres, la mission a pu constater avec intérêt et satisfaction, l’évolution du processus d’opérationnalisation de l’université ainsi que l’effort d’implication des acteurs concernés.
- Le ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, chargé de l’Instruction civique et de la Construction citoyenne a informé Conseil des ministres des rencontres destinées aux étudiants dénommées « Masterclass citoyenne ».
La « Masterclass citoyenne », organisée par le Ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports, chargé de l’Instruction civique et de la Construction citoyenne en collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, est une mission d’éducation civique, citoyenne, de développement personnel et d’engagement patriotique pour faire des étudiants des « citoyens modèles et responsables ».
Elle consiste pour le ministre chargé de la Construction citoyenne d’animer des modules sur la citoyenneté dans les universités publiques ou privées au cours de l’année universitaire 2025, en vue de renforcer le rôle des étudiants dans la refondation du Mali.
- Le ministre de l’Agriculture a informé le Conseil des ministres des conclusions de sa participation à la 19ème édition de la Bourse nationale aux Céréales.
Du 19 au 21 février 2025, le ministre de l’Agriculture à la tête d’une forte délégation a procédé au lancement officiel de la 19ème édition de la Bourse nationale aux Céréales.
A l’instar des éditions antérieures, l’objectif de cette 19ème édition était de contribuer à la promotion et à la valorisation des céréales produites localement.
En termes de bilan, l’édition de 2025 de la Bourse nationale aux Céréales a enregistré la signature de 61 contrats, pour un montant global de 1 milliard 184 millions 410 mille F CFA, contre 261 contrats d’un montant de 1 milliard 70 millions 988 mille 394 F CFA pour l’édition de 2024.
Au terme de cette édition, des recommandations ont été formulées à l’endroit du Ministère de l’Agriculture, du Commissariat à la Sécurité alimentaire et de l’Assemblée permanente des Chambres d’Agriculture du Mali.
- Le ministre de l’Entrepreneuriat national, de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle a informé le Conseil des ministres :
- du lancement du processus de recrutement des jeunes diplômés sans emploi au titre du 14ème contingent du programme de stage de formation professionnelle de l’Agence pour la Promotion de l’Emploi des Jeunes.
Le stage de formation professionnelle est un axe opérationnel de la composante I du Programme Emploi Jeunes exécuté par l’Agence pour la Promotion de l’Emploi des Jeunes.
Le lancement de l’opération de recrutement de 2 500 nouveaux stagiaires au titre du 14ème contingent du Programme de stage de formation professionnelle a débuté par le processus d’appel à candidature le 13 février 2025, suivi de l’ouverture du dépôt des candidatures le 17 février 2025.
A la date limite du dépôt des candidatures, le 22 février 2025, 15 021 dossiers ont été enregistrés sur l’ensemble du territoire national, répartis comme suit :
– 6 791 candidatures masculines, soit 45,22% ;
– 8 230 candidatures féminines, soit 54,78 %.
Après la proclamation des résultats, les nouveaux stagiaires seront affectés aux Institutions de la République, aux départements ministériels, aux Collectivités territoriales, aux organisations consulaires et faîtières ainsi qu’aux Organisations non gouvernementales.
- une mission de terrain effectuée à Gao
Une forte délégation conduite par le ministre de l’Entrepreneuriat national, de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle a effectué, du 27 février au 1er mars 2025, une mission de terrain dans la Région de Gao en vue de transmettre aux populations locales le message de réconfort, d’assurance et de solidarité des Autorités de la Transition et de recueillir leurs besoins prioritaires en matière de développement des compétences et d’insertion socioprofessionnelle, notamment des jeunes et des femmes.
Au cours de cette mission, plusieurs activités ont été menées, notamment :
– l’inauguration d’un nouveau bâtiment pour la Direction régionale de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle ;
– l’ouverture de trois Espaces d’Orientation Jeunesse ;
– le lancement de l’opération « permis de conduire » ;
– la remise de kits d’insertion aux bénéficiaires de formation dans les domaines de l’agroalimentaire, de l’électricité photovoltaïque, de la coupe-couture, de la maintenance des engins lourds.
La mission a également recueilli les attentes des acteurs locaux qui concernent, entre autres : la poursuite des initiatives en faveur de la paix et de la sécurité, l’adaptation de l’offre de formation aux besoins du marché du travail, l’accompagnement spécifique des jeunes et des femmes et la mise en place de mesures concrètes pour réduire le chômage.
- Le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce a informé le Conseil des ministres de la tenue au Mali de la 1ère édition du Forum de l’Investissement en Afrique de l’Organisation de la Coopération islamique.
Lors de sa 47ème Session tenue les 27 et 28 novembre 2020 au Niger, le Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’Organisation de la coopération islamique a décidé d’organiser pour la première fois un forum de l’Investissement en Afrique. Le Mali a été retenu pour accueillir cet événement en 2025, à l’issue d’un processus de sélection lors de la 50ème Session tenue en août 2024 à Yaoundé au Cameroun.
Ce forum dont le thème est : « Libérer le potentiel d’investissement en Afrique » a pour objectif de renforcer la coopération économique au sein de l’Organisation de la Coopération islamique et d’attirer des investisseurs en Afrique.
Plusieurs thèmes tels que le financement des investissements, les assurances et les questions de genre seront abordés lors du forum.
Le forum offre à notre pays une opportunité de promouvoir son attractivité économique et de mobiliser des investissements publics et privés.
- Le ministre de la Santé et du Développement social a informé le Conseil des ministres de la situation épidémiologique du pays marquée par une augmentation du nombre de cas confirmés de dengue comparé à celui de la semaine écoulée.
Le président de la Transition, Chef de l’Etat a appelé la population au respect strict des mesures de prévention et de lutte contre la maladie.

The Council of Ministers met in ordinary session on Wednesday 5 March 2025, in its deliberation room at the Koulouba Palace, under the chairmanship of General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State.

- At the start of the session, His Excellency General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State, prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died, offered his condolences to their families and expressed wishes for a prompt recovery to the injured, following the tragedies that occurred at the gold-panning sites at Kokoyo, in the village of Danga, Kangaba Cercle, and at Bilalikoto, Kenieba Cercle.

The Head of State instructed the Government to strengthen measures to avoid human and environmental tragedies in our country.

The President of the Transition, Head of State, further instructed:

- the repeal of the appointment orders of the administrative officials directly involved in the occurrence of the said incidents: Prefect, Sub-prefects, heads of the Security Forces (Police, Gendarmerie, Guard), of the local Water and Forestry services, the Sanitation and Pollution and Nuisance Control services, and the sub-regional Geology and Mines services;

- the revision of certain legal texts in order, among other things, to put an end to settlement procedures in the environmental field, to facilitate the recovery of equipment involved in gold panning and its transfer to the property of the State;

- the suspension of artisanal mining exploitation permits granted to persons of foreign nationality;

- the launch of the procedure for the dissolution of the Communal Council of Dabia.

- After examining the items on the agenda, the Council:

- adopted draft texts;

- and heard communications.

UNDER THE HEADING OF LEGISLATIVE AND REGULATORY MEASURES

- On the report of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the Council of Ministers adopted draft texts relating to the ratification of the Budget Support Agreement including a loan, signed in Bamako on 26 February 2025, between the Government of the Republic of Mali and the Qatar Fund for Development.

Under this agreement, the Qatar Fund for Development grants the Government of the Republic of Mali budget support in the amount of 50 million US dollars, that is approximately 31 billion 447 million 500 thousand CFA francs, comprising a loan of 45 million US dollars, that is approximately 28 billion 302 million 750 thousand CFA francs.

This budget support will make it possible to sustain the sectors of humanitarian aid, economic development and health, in particular the supply of foodstuffs, the construction of water points, the rehabilitation and construction of infrastructure and the strengthening of the means of action of the Administration and of the local authorities.

- On the report of the Minister of Economy and Finance, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance amending Law No. 06-067 of 29 December 2006, as amended, on the General Tax Code.

The Government adopted Law No. 2023-040 of 29 August 2023 on the Mining Code in the Republic of Mali in order to derive greater benefit from mining rent.

This new Code introduced into the mining framework an establishment agreement for the exploration phase and another for the exploitation phase, reduced the period of stability of the tax regime, instituted the overproduction royalty and the taxation of super-profits, increased the State's participation in the capital of mining exploitation companies and abolished customs exemptions during the exploitation phase.

It also introduced progressivity in the rate of the ad valorem tax and allowed the conclusion of memoranda of understanding between the Government of the Republic of Mali and mining companies.

The draft ordinance, adopted, amends articles 240 and 425 with a view to adapting the General Tax Code to the new Mining Code.

This amendment brings the following innovations:

- the extension of the scope of application of the Special Tax on Certain Products to marble, gold ingots and other mining products;

- the reduction of the minimum rate of the Special Tax on Certain Products for marble, gold ingots and other mining products from 5% to 3%;

- the extension of stamp duty on export intentions to all mining products.

- On the report of the Minister of Health and Social Development, the Council of Ministers adopted:

- a draft decree setting the deadlines and the procedures for the conclusion of agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health providers.

The process led, after the establishment of the Compulsory Health Insurance Scheme and the Medical Assistance Scheme, to the adoption of Law No. 2018-074 of 31 December 2018 instituting the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

The implementation of Universal Health Insurance requires a contracting system that clearly defines the deadlines and the procedures for the conclusion of agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health providers.

Thus, Decree No. 10-577/P-RM of 26 October 2010 setting the deadlines and the procedures for the conclusion of agreements between health providers and the National Health Insurance Fund was adopted for the implementation of the Compulsory Health Insurance Scheme.

The application of this decree revealed shortcomings within the framework of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme which need to be corrected in order to extend, in particular, coverage to all categories of workers.

The draft decree, adopted, will make it possible to organise effectively the coverage of all insured persons and beneficiaries of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

- a draft decree approving the standard management-delegation agreements within the framework of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

Law No. 2018-074 of 31 December 2018 instituting the Universal Health Insurance Scheme provides for the possibility for the National Health Insurance Fund to delegate, under its control, certain missions to delegated managing bodies and to involve commercial companies whose expertise in health risk management is proven.

The draft decree, adopted, will make it possible to put in place a mechanism to ensure the sharing, according to needs, of functions between the National Health Insurance Fund and the delegated managing bodies.

- a draft decree setting the principles of preferential pricing and the coverage rates of health care services within the framework of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

The Government instituted the Universal Health Insurance Scheme with a view to promoting the efficient pooling of resources and strategic purchasing in health care.

The functioning of universal health insurance necessarily requires certain prerequisites, among which is the clarification of the provisions relating to the establishment of preferential pricing of procedures and medicines.

The draft decree, adopted, specifies the principles of pricing and reimbursement of the services offered to all beneficiaries of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

UNDER THE HEADING OF COMMUNICATIONS

- The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation, held from 24 to 26 February 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland.

The "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation is a framework enabling Heads of State or Government or other high dignitaries to take stock of the promotion and protection of human rights in their respective countries.

Mali, through the Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, addressed the Human Rights Council to convey strong messages, in particular:

- reaffirmation of the determination of the Government of Mali to implement all of the recommendations accepted during the Universal Periodic Review and the commitments made at the high-level event "Human Rights 75";

- the remarkable improvement in the overall security situation thanks to the efforts of the Armed and Security Forces and their strategic partners;

- the pooling of defence resources by the Heads of State of the Alliance of Sahel States, with a view to fighting terrorism effectively;

- the appropriation of the endogenous resolution of multidimensional crises through the ongoing drafting of the National Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation;

- the Government's determination to fight impunity in all its forms;

- the reiteration of the appeal addressed to the international community with a view to avoiding the politicisation and instrumentalisation of human rights;

- the reaffirmation of the willingness of the Government of Mali to pursue, in strict respect for its sovereignty and the vital interests of the Malian People, its cooperation with all human rights promotion and protection mechanisms.

On the margins of the work of the "High-Level Segment", the minister had an audience with the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, on the efforts and progress in human rights in Mali, and the resumption and strengthening of relations of cooperation between Mali and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.

- The Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his mission to Timbuktu from 25 to 27 February 2025.

The objectives of this mission were, among others:

- to ascertain the state of progress of the operationalisation of the University of Timbuktu in order to identify the actions and measures to be undertaken;

- to exchange with the administrative, customary and educational authorities with a view to providing appropriate avenues of solution to the challenges linked to the operationalisation of the University of Timbuktu;

- to visit the site earmarked for the construction of the University's infrastructure.

Within the framework of the effective start-up of the University of Timbuktu, the department proceeded with the appointment of the Coordinator in charge of the university's operationalisation activities, the renovation of certain administrative and teaching premises and the holding of the first session of the Board of Directors of the Ahmed Baba Institute of Higher Islamic Studies and Research of Timbuktu, a component of the said university.

Through the various meetings, the mission was able to note with interest and satisfaction the progress of the university's operationalisation process as well as the effort to involve the actors concerned.

- The Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building, informed the Council of Ministers of the meetings intended for students called "Citizen Masterclass".

The "Citizen Masterclass", organised by the Ministry of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building, in collaboration with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, is a mission of civic and citizenship education, personal development and patriotic engagement aimed at making students "model and responsible citizens".

It consists, for the minister in charge of Citizen Building, of delivering modules on citizenship in public or private universities during the 2025 academic year, with a view to strengthening the role of students in the refoundation of Mali.

- The Minister of Agriculture informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his participation in the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange.

From 19 to 21 February 2025, the Minister of Agriculture, at the head of a large delegation, proceeded with the official launch of the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange.

Like previous editions, the objective of this 19th edition was to contribute to the promotion and valorisation of locally produced cereals.

In terms of results, the 2025 edition of the National Cereals Exchange recorded the signing of 61 contracts, for an overall amount of 1 billion 184 million 410 thousand CFA francs, compared with 261 contracts worth 1 billion 70 million 988 thousand 394 CFA francs for the 2024 edition.

At the end of this edition, recommendations were formulated for the Ministry of Agriculture, the Food Security Commission and the Permanent Assembly of Chambers of Agriculture of Mali.

- The Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training informed the Council of Ministers:

- of the launch of the process of recruiting unemployed young graduates for the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship programme of the Agency for the Promotion of Youth Employment.

The vocational training internship is an operational axis of component I of the Youth Employment Programme implemented by the Agency for the Promotion of Youth Employment.

The launch of the operation to recruit 2,500 new interns for the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship programme began with the call-for-applications process on 13 February 2025, followed by the opening of the submission of applications on 17 February 2025.

At the deadline for the submission of applications, on 22 February 2025, 15,021 files had been registered across the national territory, broken down as follows:

- 6,791 male applications, that is 45.22%;

- 8,230 female applications, that is 54.78%.

After the proclamation of the results, the new interns will be assigned to the Institutions of the Republic, to ministerial departments, to local authorities, to consular and umbrella organisations as well as to non-governmental organisations.

- of a field mission carried out in Gao.

A large delegation led by the Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training carried out, from 27 February to 1 March 2025, a field mission in the Gao Region with a view to conveying to the local populations the message of comfort, reassurance and solidarity of the Transition Authorities and to gathering their priority needs in terms of skills development and socio-professional integration, particularly of young people and women.

During this mission, several activities were carried out, notably:

- the inauguration of a new building for the Regional Directorate of Employment and Vocational Training;

- the opening of three Youth Guidance Spaces;

- the launch of the "driving licence" operation;

- the handover of integration kits to the beneficiaries of training in the fields of agri-food, photovoltaic electricity, cutting and sewing, and heavy machinery maintenance.

The mission also gathered the expectations of local actors, which concern, among other things: the continuation of initiatives in favour of peace and security, the adaptation of training provision to the needs of the labour market, specific support for young people and women, and the implementation of concrete measures to reduce unemployment.

- The Minister of Industry and Trade informed the Council of Ministers of the holding in Mali of the 1st edition of the Africa Investment Forum of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

At its 47th Session held on 27 and 28 November 2020 in Niger, the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation decided to organise for the first time an Africa Investment Forum. Mali was selected to host this event in 2025, following a selection process at the 50th Session held in August 2024 in Yaounde, Cameroon.

This forum, whose theme is "Unlocking investment potential in Africa", has as its objective to strengthen economic cooperation within the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and to attract investors to Africa.

Several themes such as investment financing, insurance and gender issues will be addressed at the forum.

The forum offers our country an opportunity to promote its economic attractiveness and to mobilise public and private investment.

- The Minister of Health and Social Development informed the Council of Ministers of the country's epidemiological situation, marked by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with that of the past week.

The President of the Transition, Head of State, called on the population to strictly respect the measures for the prevention of and the fight against the disease.

- የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት አባል ለመሆን ተስፋ ሰጪ ደረጃ ላይ መደረሱ ተነግሯል
የአፍሪካ ነፃ የንግድ ቀጣና ስምምነት በመጪው ሳምንት መስከረም 29 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. በይፋ እንደሚጀመርና ኢትዮጵያም የመጀመሪያውን ጭነት ወደ ኬንያ እንደምትልክ የንግድና ቀጠናዊ ትስስር ሚኒስቴር አስታወቀ፡፡
ሚኒስቴሩ ይህንን የገለጸው በስዊዘርላንድ ዋና ከተማ ጄኔቫ ከሰሞኑ የተካሄደውን የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት ድርድር 6ኛ የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ መጠናቀቅን አስመልክቶ፣ ሰኞ መስከረም 19 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. በሰጠው ጋዜጣዊ መግለጫ ነው፡፡
መግለጫውን የሰጡት የንግድና ቀጣናዊ ትስስር ሚኒስትር ካሳሁን ጎፌ (ዶ/ር) የአፍሪካ ነፃ የንግድ ቀጣና ስምምነት በመስከረም ወር ሁለተኛ ሳምንት ላይ በይፋ ይጀመራል ተብሎ የነበረ ቢሆንም፣ በዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት የአባልነት ድርድር ምክንያት አለመጀመሩን ገልጸዋል። በመሆኑም ስምምነቱ በሚቀጥለው ሳምንት መስከረም 29 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. መተግበር እንደሚጀመር ሚኒስትሩ ተናግረዋል፡፡ ‹‹ስምምነቱን በይፋ ማስጀመሩ ቀላል ሥራ ነው›› ያሉት ሚኒስትሩ፣ ነገር ግን አዳዲስ የባለብዙ ወገን ስምምነቶችን መፈጸም ከባዱና ፈታኝ መሆኑንና ትልቅ ሥራም እንደሚጠይቅ አስረድተዋል።
ኢትዮጵያ ቀደም ባሉት ዓመታት በቆሎና ቦሎቄ ወደ ኬንያ ስትልክ፣ ኬንያ ከአሥር እስከ 15 በመቶ ቀረጥ የምትጥል የነበረ ቢሆንም፣ ከመስከረም 29 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. ጀምሮ ሙሉ በሙሉ እንደምታነሳ ታውቋል፡፡
ስምምነቱን ከፈረሙ አገሮች ጋር በዕቃዎች ወይም በሸቀጦች ግብይት ሒደቱ እንደሚጀምር የጠቆሙት ሚኒስትሩ፣ በአገልግሎት ዘርፍ የውል መግባት ጥያቄ መቅረቡን፣ ነገር ግን ድርድሩ አለማለቁን ጠቅሰዋል። ለዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት የቀረበውን የድርድር ጥያቄ እዚሁ ላይ የሚቀርብ በመሆኑ የተለየ ነገር ይመጣል ተብሎ እንደማይታሰብ፣ ድርድሩም ዘንድሮ ይጠናቀቃል ተብሎ እንደሚጠበቅ ጠቁመዋል፡፡ የሚገኘው ገቢ ይህ ነው ተብሎ ሊገለጽ እንደማይችል፣ ነገር ግን በትግበራ ሒደት ወደፊት እንደሚታይ ተናግረዋል፡፡
በዚሁ ረገድ የሸቀጦች ግብይት ውል (Goods Offer) በሚኒስትሮች ምክር ቤት ያፀደቁ 34 አገሮች መኖራቸውን ጠቁመው፣ በስምምነቱ መሠረት ከእነዚህ አገሮች ምርቶችን የሚያስገቡ ድርጅቶች ሠርተፍኬት (Rules of Origin) ይዘው የሚመጡ ከሆነ፣ ከቀረጥ ነፃ ሆኖ እንዲገባላቸው፣ የጉምሩክ ኮሚሽንም ሰርተፊኬት እንዲሰጣቸውና እንዲስተናገዱ እንደሚደረግ ተናግረዋል።
የግል ድርጅቶች በዚሁ ስምምነት መሠረት ምርቶችን ለመላክ ዕድሎች እያመለጧቸው ስለሆነ፣ ሒደቱ ቶሎ ወደ ሥራ እንዲገባላቸውና በዚህ ማዕቀፍ ሥር መነገድ እንደሚፈልጉ ጥያቄ እያቀረቡ መሆናቸውን ሚኒስትሩ ሳይጠቅሱ አላለፉም፡፡
ይህ በዚህ እያለ ካሳሁን (ዶ/ር) በ6ኛው የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ ለድርጅቱ አባልነት የተከናወኑ ተግባራትን አብራርተዋል። በአሁኑ ወቅት የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅትን ለመቀላቀል 22 አገሮች በተለያየ የድርድር ደረጃ ላይ እንደሚገኙ፣ ከእነዚሁ አገሮችም ኢትዮጵያና ኡዝቤኪስታን ለአባልነት መቃረባቸውን ተናግረዋል። የ5ኛውን የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ ከተካሄደ በኋላ ላለፉት አምስት ወራት በርካታ ሥራዎችን በማከናወን ለ6ኛው የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ ሰፊ ዝግጅት መደረጉን፣ በዚህም ከ30 በላይ የድርጅቱ አባል አገሮች የተሳተፉበት የኢትዮጵያ የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት ፎረምና ከኢትዮጵያ ወዳጅ አገሮች ጋር ውጤታማ ውይይት መካሄዱን ገልጸዋል።
በዚህም በ6ኛው የቡድን ሥራ ላይ ከድርጅቱ አባል አገሮች መካከል 30 ያህሉ የዓለም ባንክ የኢትዮጵያን የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት አባልነትን ደግፈው ንግግር ማድረጋቸውን አስረድተዋል። በዚህ ስብሰባ ላይ የኢትዮጵያ ተደራዳሪ ኮሚቴ ከ650 በላይ ገጽ ያለው የፍሬ ነገር ሰነድ ማቅረቡንና ጠቅላላ ጉባዔው ሰነዱን ለማፅደቅ ወደ ረቂቅ ሪፖርት ደረጃ እንዲያድግ መወሰኑን፣ ይህም ትልቅ ሥራ እንደሆነ፣ በስብሰባው ከ200 በላይ ጥያቄዎች ተነስተው ምላሽ እንደተሰጠባቸውም በዝርዝር አስረድተዋል፡፡
በዚህ ስብሰባ 54 ተጨማሪ የሕግ ሰነዶች መቅረባቸውን፣ በእስካሁን ሒደት የቀረበውም 398 መድረሳቸውን ተናግረዋል። ከሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባው ጎን ለጎን በሁለትዮሽ የገበያ ዕድል ድርድር ጥያቄ ካቀረቡ 22 የድርጁቱ አባል አገሮች መካከል ከ14 ያህሉ ጋር የፊት ለፊት ውይይት መደረጉን፣ ከስድስቱ ጋር ደግሞ በቴክኒክ ደረጃ ከስምምነት መደረሱን፣ ሆኖም አራት አገሮች በተለያዩ ምክንያቶች ድርድሩን አቋርጠው መውጣታቸውንም ጠቁመዋል፡፡
ሩሲያ፣ ቻይና፣ ቱርኪዬ፣ አርጀንቲና፣ እንዲሁም ታይላንድ ስምምነት ከተደረሰባቸው አገሮች መካከል ተጠቃሽ ናቸው ያሉት ሚኒስትሩ፣ ከድርድሩ አቋርጠው የወጡ አገሮችን ስም ግን ከመግለጽ ተቆጥበዋል።
‹‹በሁለትዮሽ የገበያ ዕድል ድርድር ጥያቄ ያቀረበ አገር በአንተ ፍጥነት አልጓዝ ሲል ትቸገራለህ፣ ዶክመንት ልከኸለት አልመልስም ይላል፣ ያዘገያል፡፡ በሌላ በኩል ደግሞ ከተባለው ስታንዳርድ (ደረጃ) በታች ያቀረብኸውን ነገር ዝቅ አድርጎ የመጠየቅ ጉዳዮች አሉ፤›› ብለዋል።
ይህም የአባልነት ሒደቱ ተግዳሮት መሆኑን ጠቅሰዋል። ሆኖም ስምምነት ከተደረሰባቸው ስድስት አገሮች ጋር ከተገኘው ልምድ በመነሳት፣ በሰጥቶ መቀበል መርህ የሚደረጉ ድርድሮችን ለማጠናቀቅ እንደሚሠራ ገልጸዋል። ከስዊዘርላንድና ከጃፓን ጋር የሚደረገው ድርድር በመጪው ሳምንት ሊያልቅ እንደሚችል የጠቆሙት ካሳሁን (ዶ/ር)፣ እስከ ኅዳር 30 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. ድረስ የነቃ ድርድር እየተካሄደ ካለባቸው 14 አገሮች ጋር ከስምምነት ለመድረስ እንደሚሠራ ተናግረዋል። ከአሜሪካ ጋር የሚደረገው የባለብዙ ወገንና የሁለትዮሽ የንግድ ድርድር እስካሁን ድረስ አለመቋጨቱንና ተጠናክሮ መቀጠሉን፣ በቀጣይ ከሁለትዮሽ የገበያ ዕድል ጎን ለጎን የባለብዙ ወገን ድርድሮች መከናወናቸውን እንደሚቀጥሉ አክለዋል።
በዋናነት የኢትዮጵያን የፍሬ ነገር ሪፖርት ወደ ሥራ ቡድን ረቂቅ ሪፖርት ደረጃ ማደጉ፣ ለዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት አባልነት እየተደረገ ላለው ሒደት ተስፋ ሰጪ መሆኑን አስምረውበታል። ከዚህ አንፃር 6ኛው የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ ውጤታማ ሆኖ መጠናቀቁን የጠቀሱት ሚኒስትሩ፣ 7ኛው የሥራ ቡድን ስብሰባ በመጪው ጥር 2018 ዓ.ም. ለማካሄድ ቀጠሮ መያዙን፣ የዓለም ንግድ ድርጅት ድርድር እ.ኤ.አ. በመጋቢት 2026 በካሜሩን በሚካሄደው 14ኛው የድርጅቱ የሚኒስትሮች ጉባዔ ላይ ለማጠናቀቅ ታቅዶ እየተሠራ መሆኑን አስታውቀዋል፡፡
a1761.en:
It was announced that Ethiopia will begin sending its first shipment next week under the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement

- It has been reported that a promising stage has been reached toward becoming a member of the World Trade Organization

The Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration announced that the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement will officially begin next week, on Meskerem 29, 2018 E.C., and that Ethiopia will send its first shipment to Kenya.

The Ministry stated this at a press briefing given on Monday, Meskerem 19, 2018 E.C., marking the conclusion of the 6th Working Party meeting of the World Trade Organization negotiations, held recently in Geneva, the capital of Switzerland.

The Minister of Trade and Regional Integration, Kassahun Gofe (PhD), who gave the briefing, explained that although the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement had been expected to be officially launched in the second week of Meskerem, it did not begin because of the World Trade Organization membership negotiations. Accordingly, the minister said the agreement will begin to be implemented next week, on Meskerem 29, 2018 E.C. "Officially launching the agreement is an easy task," said the minister, but he explained that concluding new multilateral agreements is the difficult and challenging part and that it requires a great deal of work.
