Claro que somos impactados pelo que acontece no mundo, em particular na Europa, no comércio externo, no investimento directo estrangeiro, na origem dos turistas, nas remessas onde se acrescentam as dos EUA. Por natureza o empresário tem de ser optimista, com os pés assentes no chão, ou seja, realista e pragmático. E é possível para quem está a produzir bens e serviços, aqui em Cabo Verde, estar concentrado nesta realidade.
Há pouco estava a falar de onde estávamos a partir do cenário macroeconómico cabo-verdiano e onde é que podemos chegar?
O desempenho económico do país tem sido relativamente robusto nos anos mais recentes depois de ter um crescimento de apenas cerca de 1% em média entre os anos de 2009 a 2015. Em 2016 a taxa de crescimento foi de 4,3% e o crescimento médio anual entre 2016 e 2019 foi de 4,9%, tendo mesmo crescido cerca de 7% no ano 2019 (Dados do FMI). Em 2020, com a COVID, sofremos a maior contração económica da nossa história (-22,8%), a segunda maior contração em África. Os anos de 2021 e 2022 são atípicos porque acontecem na recuperação pós-COVID. Em 2023 voltámos (5,1%) às taxas que aconteceram entre 2016 e 2019. Bons números que comparam bem em termos internacionais, naturalmente com a ambição de aumentarem num futuro próximo. Naturalmente, o PIB não é o único indicador, havendo outros como o Índice de Desenvolvimento Humano, que também evoluiu favoravelmente depois da crise COVID. Mas não há dúvida de que o PIB, ou seja, a riqueza criada no país em cada ano, continua a ser o indicador mais importante do desempenho das economias. É certo que a dívida pública atingiu níveis estratosféricos em resultado da crise, que a levou para números acima de 150% do PIB. Em 2024 passou para os 110% do PIB, o que revela uma recuperação notável. A taxa de inflação, depois de décadas em números muito baixos de um a dois por cento, de que fomos grandes beneficiários em termos de estabilidade de preços e do que isso traz de forma decisiva à economia; no pós-COVID e principalmente após o início da guerra na Ucrânia a taxa de inflação subiu muito fixando-se em 5,4% em 2021 com um pico em 2022 de 7,6%. A partir de 2023 voltámos ao normal com uma taxa de 1,3% e a estimativa para 2024 é que fique nos 2%. Claro que como somos uma micro-economia com uma grande componente de importação e a inflação dos nossos principais parceiros repercute-se quase directamente no país atendendo ao nosso regime de câmbio fixo. Diria que em termos macroeconómicos, e para já, as coisas vão bem. Claro que existem riscos, em especial devido à nossa vulnerabilidade e ainda existem os constrangimentos, as dificuldades, os problemas, alguns persistentes, que devem ser resolvidos para libertar todo o nosso potencial de crescimento e criarmos uma economia e sociedade mais próspera e com maior qualidade de vida para todos, sabendo que temos franjas significativas da população em situação abaixo das condições mínimas de dignidade humana.
Que perspectivas para o sector da construção civil?
O sector continua a ser relevante na economia com o seu peso de cerca de 10% no PIB, e no volume de emprego que gera. Para além de dinamizar um conjunto de outros subsectores económicos a montante, como todos os fornecedores de bens e serviços que incorpora na sua produção. Por outro lado, encontramos diferentes segmentos de mercado: o das obras públicas e o da construção, digamos, imobiliária, que por sua vez ainda se poderia dividir em subsegmentos. E as características desses segmentos de mercado são diferentes. Falando do subsector das obras públicas e enquanto presidente da ACEC e apenas concentrando-me nos anos recentes, porque alguns dos problemas de hoje resultam de opções e políticas erradas que se tomaram na década de 2000. E falar sobre isso daria pano para manga e uma entrevista dedicada a esse histórico. Destacaria dois assuntos relevantes:
a. O sector foi muito fustigado pela elevada inflação que se seguiu no pós-Covid e se agravou com a guerra da Ucrânia e as empresas viram-se confrontadas com um aumento vertiginoso dos materiais, energia e transportes. O problema é que as obras públicas são por preço fixo não revisível. Felizmente foi possível, demorando mais tempo do que deveria aprovar lei temporária que permitiu às empresas atenuar os custos adicionais que resultaram dessa alta de preços;
b. O Dono de Obra público deve fazer um maior investimento na melhoria técnica dos projectos colocados a concurso público. Um deficiente projecto de execução traz sempre problemas ao dono de obra e em particular à empresa executora. Compreende-se que haja interesse em lançar o concurso com a maior brevidade para conseguir os impactos positivos, mas isso não deve ser feito porque os impactos negativos são de monta. Um bom projecto é sempre meio caminho andado na execução de uma obra. Não digo que isso seja generalizado, há muitos casos em que os projectos colocados a concurso são de boa qualidade, ou são de responsabilidade do empreiteiro onde essa situação não se coloca. Mas continua a acontecer vezes de mais e deve ser corrigido. Claro que ainda existem muitas outras questões que podiam ser abordadas sobre o sector da construção, mas sei que o espaço é limitado.
Como analisa a subida das taxas de juro e que impacto se pode prever no financiamento das empresas?
Sobre o sistema financeiro foi publicado um estudo sectorial cobrindo um período alargado, de 2015 a 2023, elaborado pela PD Consult, do Paulino Dias, e que traça a evolução e faz um retrato do conjunto e de cada um dos bancos a operar em Cabo Verde nesse período e ajuda a entender melhor um sector tão vital para qualquer economia. Muito sinceramente e a não ser por alguma outra razão que me escape, não vejo que traga problemas de maior a não ser numa ligeira pressão para a subida das taxas de juros praticadas pelos bancos em relação às empresas e famílias. Isto deve-se aos seguintes factos:
a. O nosso sistema financeiro e em particular monetário tem peculiaridades que resultam da nossa dimensão e escala, onde historicamente as alterações de taxas directoras por parte do BCV não levam a alterações de monta nas taxas de juros médias nas operações de crédito às empresas e famílias;
b. No período de 2015 a 2023, as taxas médias de juros praticadas estiveram num intervalo pequeno próximo dos 9%, com excepção de dois anos excepcionais, o de 2016 e 2017 onde baixaram para os 7,9% e 6,9%; infelizmente essa excelente tendência de baixa não se manteve e em 2018 voltou a subir aos 8% a que se seguiu um pico anormal de 11% em 2019, regressando ao intervalo perto de 9% a partir daí de 2020 até 2023;
c. Os bancos depois de alguns anos de agruras em que tiveram rentabilidades baixas, em que até houve a proibição de distribuição de dividendos por parte do BCV, voltaram aos lucros e a uma boa rentabilidade, os indicadores de solvência melhoraram muito e todos os bancos e o sistema no seu todo está a consolidar-se. E bancos saudáveis e rentáveis é o que todos precisamos na economia. Espera-se que os bancos beneficiem de margens confortáveis – a diferença entre as taxas a que emprestam dinheiro aos clientes e as taxas muito baixas que remuneram os depósitos dos clientes. O nível actual das taxas é suficientemente bom para os bancos porque está a proporcionar-lhes uma boa rentabilidade. Não há nenhuma razão para essas taxas serem aumentadas.
Que sectores poderão ter maior crescimento este ano?
Valerá a pena conhecer um pouco do que é a estrutura da economia cabo-verdiana. O turismo tem um peso enorme, 25% do PIB, e garante 25% dos empregos formais. Diria que em 2025 continuará a ser esse o nosso motor de crescimento arrastando todos os outros sectores e sub-sectores. Mas em termos de alteração de estrutura das contribuições sectoriais para o PIB, os efeitos das reformas e politicas só se fazem sentir num médio prazo, entre três e cinco anos.
E em termos de oportunidades. Onde estarão elas?
O Banco Mundial em estudo recente de 2024 intitulado “Criando Mercados em Cabo Verde” faz um diagnóstico do sector privado e identifica os motores de crescimento, os desafios e as oportunidades. Essas oportunidades, algumas delas de nichos, são nos sectores: do turismo, da economia azul – ou economia do mar – e nos serviços digitais, sabendo-se que ter-se-iam de resolver as questões da concorrência e do ambiente regulamentar, as questões do transporte e da logística e as questões da energia, que constituem os grandes constrangimentos, para conseguirmos um sector privado, de capital nacional ou internacional, que tenha bons negócios, com rentabilidade adequadas para garantir os reinvestimentos sempre necessários e a devida remuneração do capital investido.
Por falar em Banco Mundial e em economia, a instituição também veio dizer que o modelo de desenvolvimento cabo-verdiano está esgotado pelo menos desde 2008. Como é que os empresários vêem estas conclusões?
A sua pergunta fez-me lembrar de uma entrevista que tinha dado ao Expresso das Ilhas em 2016, e que revi, cujo título era: “É preciso mudarmos o modelo de desenvolvimento económico ou não garantimos o mínimo de prosperidade para todos”. Outros já o tinham dito em anos anteriores, até em décadas passadas como o saudoso Eugénio Inocêncio, que no início dos anos noventa já tinha dito que tínhamos de deixar de ser uma economia de reciclagem de ajuda externa para passarmos a ser uma economia produtiva. E esse continua a ser o maior desafio de Cabo Verde ainda hoje. Pela nossa dimensão, dispersão, escala (ou falta dela), a nossa economia debate-se à partida com condições de base difíceis e desafiantes. Temos vários casos de falhas de mercado que têm de ser atendidas. Caracterizaria a estrutura do mercado do lado da oferta, que em grande parte é o possível ou o viável, ou seja, as empresas que fornecem os bens e serviços, nalguns casos, públicos, e que situação encontramos? Temos situações de monopólios, duopólios e oligopólios. Encontramos um monopólio, ou seja, só um operador, nos sectores da energia, nos portos, na gestão de aeroportos. Na situação de duopólios, ou seja, apenas dois operadores num sector, temos os sectores das comunicações, da água, o farmacêutico, os combustíveis e dos seguros. Isso cria distorções, que resultam da nossa própria realidade, realidade física, por estarmos dispersos em ilhas, por haver determinados sectores que, à partida, são monopólios naturais, ou seja, tem de ser o Estado, ou as entidades públicas, a investir para oferecer um bem público, de acesso universal e eventualmente básico para a vida, como energia, ou água. Isso cria dificuldades: aumentam as ineficiências, continuamos a ter um peso muito grande do sector público empresarial, aliás, não há relatório de instituições internacionais, que habitualmente, acompanham a economia cabo-verdiana, que não se referira a isso.
Continuando no Banco Mundial, a instituição também veio falar de um problema que todos os empresários cabo-verdianos já conhecem há muitos anos que é a questão da baixa produtividade em Cabo Verde. Há soluções para alterar este cenário?
Aqui, realmente dou um grande suspiro. No sentido em que, a curto prazo, diria que não. A curtíssimo prazo, temos de trabalhar para conseguir isso num futuro a médio prazo. Investir no capital humano, na educação. Há coisas positivas, por exemplo, o próprio Ministério da Educação tem como objetivo começarmos a fazer aqueles testes internacionais que avaliam determinadas competências essenciais dos alunos, no sentido de projetarmos atingir os níveis dos países avançados ou próximo disso. Estou a começar por falar das crianças e jovens porque é o que verdadeiramente alterará o país de forma estruturante. Por outro lado, o investimento nas áreas STEM, acrónimo em inglês de ciência e tecnologia, engenharia e matemáticas, que claramente dão uma outra base para a inovação e para investigação. Depois, há a questão da saída de mão-de-obra, que tem constituído um grande problema para as empresas, agravado muitos nestes últimos anos; naturalmente os que emigram, se não são os mais qualificados, são os mais ativos, com mais ambição, que não se importam de correr riscos. Também há questões ligadas às próprias empresas, públicas ou privadas, que influenciam a produtividade, como a organização, a necessidade de modernização da gestão, adoptando medidas que favoreçam o aumento da produtividade que é essencial para ao mesmo tempo aumentar o rendimento; essas duas variáveis estão ligadas; há ainda os constrangimentos como por exemplo os transportes marítimos inter-ilhas, a excessiva dependência das importações e nos sectores onde se depende da rapidez com que as encomendas são satisfeitas esperamos encomendas que demoram a chegar, e quase nunca no prazo previsto, obrigando a paragens não desejadas. E se um ou mais equipamentos estão parados por falta de peças a produtividade, naturalmente, cai muito. Os custos dos fatores de produção que são altos, parcialmente resultado da nossa realidade de que não conseguimos fugir, também ajudam a esse ambiente de baixa produtividade. Por último continuamos a ter uma administração pública que também tem problemas relativamente à sua produtividade e a sua ineficiência e ineficácia na entrega dos resultados que se propõe, de certa forma, contamina o país, a economia e as empresas, públicas ou privadas.
Por falar da perda de mão-de-obra, segundo números oficiais, em 2023, por exemplo, Portugal concedeu cerca de 5 mil vistos de trabalho a cabo-verdianos, mais do que nos 4 anos anteriores. Provavelmente está aqui uma dinâmica que vai ser difícil de contrabalançar nos próximos tempos. Ou seja, as empresas cabo-verdianas vão ter problemas em conseguir manter os seus melhores funcionários.
Esse problema já está a acontecer. Já aconteceu. Essa gente saiu e é evidente que isso já é – e sei-o por falar com várias empresas de diferentes sectores – um problema grande. Talvez tenha que se compreender um pouquinho a realidade, a Europa, e em particular Portugal, tem este problema de défice de mão-de-obra já há alguns anos. Os próprios empresários portugueses há muitos anos que vinham pressionando para que se facilitasse a entrada. Esta grande migração resulta, portanto, de uma grande procura de gente, para suprir necessidades imediatas. E estando nos genes do cabo-verdiano emigrar à procura de melhores condições de vida, é legítimo que se aspire a melhor vida, a maior rendimento. Claro que se houvesse em Cabo Verde atividades de maior valor acrescentado, que permitissem gerar outros rendimentos, estou certo que as empresas seriam as primeiras a pagar salários maiores. Mas esta migração em massa, é indiscutível, constitui um problema. A aposta com maior possibilidade futura é nós conseguirmos, aqui dentro, gerar economia suficiente, rendimento suficiente, empresas suficientes que permitam que os salários sejam atrativos e não compense emigrar, pelo menos em termos materiais. A ambição do país, da sociedade deverá ser essa.
Quando fala de melhores empresas, melhores salários, que reformas económicas poderão impactar nas empresas? Isto se as há, ou então quais seriam as necessárias em termos de prioridade?
É indiscutível que este governo adoptou outra postura em relação ao sector privado, com um ambiente mais amigável. Há algumas reformas em curso num sentido positivo. Também há uma visão estratégica para o país, de um país plataforma que preste serviços ao exterior. Se os objectivos forem realistas e estiverem dentro das nossas capacidades essa visão está correcta e poderá trazer mais desenvolvimento ao país. Que outras reformas ajudarão ao crescimento? Que o sector público empresarial funcione melhor, que ofereça serviços a tempo e de maior qualidade. Os investimentos em algumas infraestruturas, Deus nos livre dos investimentos feitos nas décadas de 2000, muitos deles transformaram-se em elefantes brancos e estão a pesar na nossa dívida pública. Diria que investimentos em infraestruturas, mas com uma perspectiva selectiva: a área dos serviços digitais como, por exemplo, as fintechs; a forma como os próprios serviços do Estado tratam o investimento direto estrangeiro e continuar a aprofundar o que tem sido o motor do nosso desenvolvimento, mas numa perspectiva em que os grandes hotéis aumentem as ligações com a economia local.
E em termos de desafios, qual acha que serão os maiores que os empresários vão enfrentar em 2025?
Fora os do mundo, porque sobre esses a gente não sabe nada, dos outros diria que são os habituais: os transportes inter-ilhas, seja os aéreos, seja os marítimos. Analisando os dados dos passageiros dos transportes aéreos, contando passageiros embarcados e desembarcados, no transporte internacional, em 2023, atingimos 2 milhões de passageiros e nesse ano conseguimos recuperar e ultrapassar o nível pré-pandemia de 2019, que era de 1,9 milhões de passageiros. Em 2024, em termos de total de passageiros, domésticos e internacionais, conseguiu-se atingir 3 milhões de passageiros, quando em 2019 tinha sido de 2,7 milhões. Sobre o transporte aéreo interno, e apenas na condição de observador externo e a partir das notícias que chegam ao público, diria que perdemos uma oportunidade com a Binter, que esteve no mercado durante poucos anos. Os números, quanto a mim, são suficientemente elucidativos. No transporte doméstico e internacional, vínhamos de 698 mil passageiros transportados, quando digo passageiros digo sempre embarcados e desembarcados, que são habitualmente os números que se utilizam, 698 mil em 2015. Em 2016, 715 mil, tudo isto com os TACV. E depois nos três anos em que a Binter está sozinha no mercado e não há Covid, que é 2017, 2018 e 2019, a Binter consegue transportar 959 mil em 2017, 884 mil em 2018 e 821 mil em 2019. É a época de ouro em termos de passageiros domésticos. Entretanto chega a COVID em 2020 e os números baixam para 249 mil, mantendo-se nos 287 mil em 2021 ainda na recuperação pós-covid e resultado das exigências como os testes aos passageiros. A partir de 2022, sem a Binter que tinha saído do mercado no início de 2021, os números voltam a crescer atingindo os 494 mil e crescem outra vez em 2023 para os 549 mil. Mas com todos os problemas que o operador que esteve a actuar no mercado teve, seria expectável conseguir números mais altos nesses anos. Ficou, por certo, parte da procura por satisfazer. Em 2024, e apesar da saída do operador anterior logo no inicio do ano e a entrada dos TACV só a partir de Março de 2024 e de uma forma tímida com pouca oferta foi possível atingir a cifra de 612 mil passageiros domésticos transportados, o que já é um número expressivo atendendo a que só nos últimos meses de 2024 os TACV tiveram um número de aviões suficiente para dar vazão à procura. Voltando à questão da Binter, eu como observador externo não percebi a razão para o governo não ter apostado em ficar com a participação de 30% que foi prevista no acordo com a Binter mais a possibilidade de o governo comprar 19%. Admito que, em termos de finanças públicas, naquela altura, e com os problemas graves herdados não houvesse essa apetência do governo para comprar e, portanto, colocar mais recursos públicos no sector, até pela situação desastrosa em que estava o negócio doméstico. Tinham-se “vendido” os aviões ATR que já estavam amortizados em mais de 70% ao fornecedor, voltando a aluga-los perdendo-se a “propriedade” que já se tinha. Essa foi uma opção ruinosa da administração da altura, sancionada pelo governo. Apenas com o objectivo de maquilhar as contas. Voltando à Binter, a participação de 30% para o Estado, que não implicava a utilização de recursos públicos, claramente devia ter sido tomada. Desconheço o que se terá passado para os levar a tomar uma atitude tão radical de abandonar o mercado, mas à partida tendo feito essa aposta durante alguns anos é provável que se tivessem um ambiente favorável e tendo eles provado que é possível manter uma operação doméstica viável, eficiente e rentável no país poderia ter-se encontrado uma forma de os manter no país. Não sei se teriam pretensões inaceitáveis, mas é só ver os números para constatar que o rombo da Covid em 2020 foi enorme. E a aviação foi particularmente afectada. Costumo dizer que este governo funciona melhor nas emergências do que no que é rotineiro. Com mais foco e energia. Isso passou-se na COVID com as políticas e medidas atempadas e assertivas que se tomaram em todas as áreas, mas em particular na saúde e nas medidas económicas que permitiram recuperar o país em termos sanitários e económicos. E isso foi conseguido em tempo recorde. Outro exemplo de sucesso deste governo, também numa situação de emergência, foi a solução que se encontrou em curto espaço de tempo com a reactivação dos TACV nos transportes aéreos domésticos. Claro que com aviões alugados incluindo tripulação é uma solução transitória porque tem custos incomportáveis e terá de se caminhar para uma solução definitiva. Vivemos momentos de verdadeira crise no sector, em particular em 2023 em que estivemos em risco de ficar sem conexão aérea entre as ilhas. Uma situação muito grave. E conseguiu-se ultrapassar isso com uma oferta neste momento estabilizada e das minhas ultimas experiências e do que tenho ouvido a funcionar bem no geral, até em relação aos atrasos e/ou cancelamentos que terão diminuído bastante. E isso é um descanso para todos: para os empresários, para as famílias, mesmo para os turistas que utilizam cada vez mais as conexões internas. Em relação ao transporte marítimo, para mim, há um pecado original no concurso que foi lançado: ter-se exigido cinco navios praticamente novos, menos de 15 anos, para operar neste nosso mercado tão estreito e exíguo. Nós estivemos no sector do transporte marítimo em Inter-ilhas, entre 2003 e 2009, e muito sinceramente não vejo que o mercado comportasse a necessidade de cinco navios e o investimento necessário para ter esses cinco navios com menos de 15 anos é de tal forma significativo que não há anos que cheguem para amortizar, ou seja, não permite a recuperação do investimento.
Texto originalmente publicado na edição impressa do Expresso das Ilhas nº 1210 de 5 de Fevereiro de 2025.
a6817.en:
From the businesspeople's point of view. What do you think the economic trend for 2025 will be?

The world is living through a very complex moment of great uncertainty. And everything that happens in the world has an impact on our little crumb, on our little grain of earth that we are here in Cabo Verde. As for the outlook for 2025, it will be worth taking stock of where we are starting from. The macroeconomic variables have performed well, there are substantial improvements after the blow that was Covid, which in 2020 meant a contraction of the economy of 20.8%, and we have been recovering and the prospects are positive/moderate. We are a micro country, a micro-economy, dispersed, with vulnerabilities and very dependent on certain sectors, as even the Covid and post-Covid crisis itself revealed.

You mentioned an important issue: 2025 is a year of uncertainty. Another one. How does one manage to plan in this environment of so much indeterminacy?

As we are enclosed within a very particular reality and there is knowledge and experience of the country, it is possible to plan, there always being unforeseen events that can happen. Of course we are impacted by what happens in the world, in particular in Europe, in foreign trade, in foreign direct investment, in the origin of tourists, in remittances, to which those from the USA are added. By nature the businessman has to be optimistic, with his feet firmly on the ground, that is, realistic and pragmatic. And that is possible for whoever is producing goods and services here in Cabo Verde, being focused on this reality.

A moment ago you were talking about where we were starting from in the Cape Verdean macroeconomic scenario – and where can we get to?

The country's economic performance has been relatively robust in the most recent years after having growth of only about 1% on average between the years 2009 and 2015. In 2016 the growth rate was 4.3% and average annual growth between 2016 and 2019 was 4.9%, having even grown about 7% in the year 2019 (IMF data). In 2020, with COVID, we suffered the greatest economic contraction in our history (-22.8%), the second largest contraction in Africa. The years 2021 and 2022 are atypical because they happen in the post-COVID recovery. In 2023 we returned (5.1%) to the rates that occurred between 2016 and 2019. Good numbers that compare well in international terms, naturally with the ambition of increasing in the near future. Naturally, GDP is not the only indicator, there being others such as the Human Development Index, which also evolved favourably after the COVID crisis. But there is no doubt that GDP, that is, the wealth created in the country each year, continues to be the most important indicator of the performance of economies. It is true that public debt reached stratospheric levels as a result of the crisis, which took it to figures above 150% of GDP. In 2024 it moved to 110% of GDP, which reveals a remarkable recovery. The inflation rate, after decades at very low figures of one to two per cent, of which we were great beneficiaries in terms of price stability and of what that decisively brings to the economy, rose a great deal post-COVID and mainly after the start of the war in Ukraine, settling at 5.4% in 2021 with a peak in 2022 of 7.6%. From 2023 we returned to normal with a rate of 1.3% and the estimate for 2024 is that it will stay at 2%. Of course, as we are a micro-economy with a large import component, the inflation of our main partners is passed on almost directly to the country given our fixed exchange rate regime. I would say that in macroeconomic terms, and for now, things are going well. Of course there are risks, especially due to our vulnerability, and there still exist the constraints, the difficulties, the problems, some persistent, that must be resolved in order to release all our growth potential and create a more prosperous economy and society with greater quality of life for all, knowing that we have significant fringes of the population in a situation below the minimum conditions of human dignity.

What prospects for the construction sector?

The sector continues to be relevant in the economy with its weight of about 10% of GDP, and in the volume of employment it generates. Besides stimulating a set of other upstream economic sub-sectors, such as all the suppliers of goods and services that it incorporates into its production. On the other hand, we find different market segments: that of public works and that of, let us say, real-estate construction, which in turn could still be divided into sub-segments. And the characteristics of these market segments are different. Speaking of the public works sub-sector and as president of ACEC, and concentrating only on recent years – because some of today's problems result from wrong choices and policies taken in the decade of the 2000s, and talking about that would give plenty of material and an interview dedicated to that history – I would highlight two relevant matters:

a. The sector was badly battered by the high inflation that followed post-Covid and that worsened with the war in Ukraine, and companies found themselves confronted with a dizzying increase in materials, energy and transport. The problem is that public works are at a fixed, non-revisable price. Fortunately it was possible, taking longer than it should have, to approve a temporary law that allowed companies to mitigate the additional costs that resulted from that rise in prices;

b. The public Works Owner should make a greater investment in the technical improvement of the projects put out to public tender. A deficient execution project always brings problems to the works owner and in particular to the executing company. It is understandable that there is an interest in launching the tender as quickly as possible in order to achieve the positive impacts, but that should not be done because the negative impacts are considerable. A good project is always half the road travelled in the execution of a work. I am not saying this is generalised; there are many cases in which the projects put out to tender are of good quality, or are the contractor's responsibility, where that situation does not arise. But it continues to happen too often and must be corrected. Of course there are still many other questions that could be addressed about the construction sector, but I know space is limited.

How do you analyse the rise in interest rates and what impact can be foreseen on company financing?

On the financial system a sectoral study was published covering an extended period, from 2015 to 2023, prepared by PD Consult, of Paulino Dias, which traces the evolution and portrays the whole and each one of the banks operating in Cabo Verde in that period and helps to better understand a sector so vital to any economy. Very sincerely, and unless for some other reason that escapes me, I do not see that it brings any major problems other than a slight pressure for a rise in the interest rates charged by the banks to companies and families. This is due to the following facts:

a. Our financial and in particular monetary system has peculiarities that result from our dimension and scale, where historically changes in key rates by the BCV [Bank of Cabo Verde] do not lead to major changes in average interest rates on credit operations to companies and families;

b. In the period from 2015 to 2023, the average interest rates charged were within a small range close to 9%, with the exception of two exceptional years, 2016 and 2017, when they fell to 7.9% and 6.9%; unfortunately that excellent downward trend did not hold and in 2018 it rose again to 8%, followed by an abnormal peak of 11% in 2019, returning to the range near 9% from then on, from 2020 to 2023;

c. The banks, after some years of hardship in which they had low profitability, in which there was even a prohibition on the distribution of dividends by the BCV, have returned to profits and to good profitability, the solvency indicators have improved a great deal and all the banks and the system as a whole are consolidating. And healthy and profitable banks are what we all need in the economy. The banks are expected to benefit from comfortable margins – the difference between the rates at which they lend money to clients and the very low rates at which they remunerate clients' deposits. The current level of rates is good enough for the banks because it is providing them with good profitability. There is no reason for those rates to be increased.

Which sectors may have the greatest growth this year?

It will be worth knowing a little of what the structure of the Cape Verdean economy is. Tourism has an enormous weight, 25% of GDP, and guarantees 25% of formal jobs. I would say that in 2025 that will continue to be our engine of growth, dragging all the other sectors and sub-sectors along. But in terms of a change in the structure of sectoral contributions to GDP, the effects of reforms and policies are only felt in the medium term, between three and five years.

And in terms of opportunities. Where will they be?

The World Bank, in a recent 2024 study entitled “Creating Markets in Cabo Verde”, makes a diagnosis of the private sector and identifies the engines of growth, the challenges and the opportunities. Those opportunities, some of them niche, are in the sectors of: tourism, the blue economy – or sea economy – and digital services, it being known that the questions of competition and the regulatory environment, the questions of transport and logistics and the questions of energy, which constitute the major constraints, would have to be resolved in order for us to achieve a private sector, of national or international capital, that has good businesses, with adequate profitability to guarantee the always necessary reinvestment and the due remuneration of the invested capital.

Speaking of the World Bank and the economy, the institution also came to say that the Cape Verdean development model has been exhausted at least since 2008. How do businesspeople see these conclusions?

Your question reminded me of an interview I had given to Expresso das Ilhas in 2016, which I reviewed, whose title was: “We need to change the model of economic development or we will not guarantee a minimum of prosperity for all”. Others had already said it in previous years, even in past decades, like the late Eugénio Inocêncio, who at the beginning of the nineties had already said that we had to stop being an economy of recycling foreign aid in order to become a productive economy. And that continues to be Cabo Verde's greatest challenge even today. Because of our dimension, dispersion, scale (or lack of it), our economy struggles from the outset with difficult and challenging base conditions. We have various cases of market failures that have to be attended to. I would characterise the structure of the market on the supply side, which is largely what is possible or viable, that is, the companies that supply goods and services, in some cases public ones – and what situation do we find? We have situations of monopolies, duopolies and oligopolies. We find a monopoly, that is, only one operator, in the sectors of energy, ports, and airport management. In the situation of duopolies, that is, only two operators in a sector, we have the sectors of communications, water, pharmaceuticals, fuels and insurance. That creates distortions, which result from our own reality, physical reality, because we are dispersed across islands, because there are certain sectors that are, from the outset, natural monopolies, that is, it has to be the State, or public entities, that invest to offer a public good, of universal access and possibly basic to life, such as energy or water. That creates difficulties: inefficiencies increase, we continue to have a very large weight of the state business sector – indeed, there is no report by international institutions that habitually follow the Cape Verdean economy that does not refer to that.

Continuing with the World Bank, the institution also spoke of a problem that all Cape Verdean businesspeople have known for many years, which is the question of low productivity in Cabo Verde. Are there solutions to change this scenario?

Here, really, I let out a big sigh. In the sense that, in the short term, I would say no. In the very short term, we have to work to achieve that in a medium-term future. Invest in human capital, in education. There are positive things; for example, the Ministry of Education itself has as an objective that we start doing those international tests that assess certain essential competences of students, with a view to projecting reaching the levels of advanced countries or close to that. I am starting by talking about children and young people because that is what will truly change the country in a structural way. On the other hand, investment in the STEM areas, the English acronym for science and technology, engineering and mathematics, which clearly give another base for innovation and research. Then there is the question of the outflow of labour, which has constituted a big problem for companies, much aggravated in these last years; naturally those who emigrate, if they are not the most qualified, are the most active, with most ambition, who do not mind taking risks. There are also questions linked to the companies themselves, public or private, that influence productivity, such as organisation, the need to modernise management, adopting measures that favour the increase in productivity which is essential in order at the same time to increase income; those two variables are linked; there are also constraints such as, for example, inter-island maritime transport, the excessive dependence on imports, and in the sectors where one depends on the speed with which orders are fulfilled we wait for orders that take time to arrive, and almost never within the expected deadline, forcing undesired stoppages. And if one or more pieces of equipment are stopped for lack of parts, productivity naturally falls a great deal. The costs of factors of production, which are high, partly a result of our reality from which we cannot escape, also contribute to that environment of low productivity. Lastly, we continue to have a public administration that also has problems regarding its productivity, and its inefficiency and ineffectiveness in delivering the results it proposes, in a way, contaminates the country, the economy and companies, public or private.

Speaking of the loss of labour, according to official figures, in 2023, for example, Portugal granted about 5,000 work visas to Cape Verdeans, more than in the previous 4 years. There is probably a dynamic here that will be difficult to counterbalance in the coming times. That is, Cape Verdean companies are going to have problems managing to keep their best employees.

That problem is already happening. It has already happened. Those people left and it is clear that this is already – and I know it from talking with several companies in different sectors – a big problem. Perhaps one has to understand the reality a little: Europe, and Portugal in particular, has had this problem of a labour deficit for some years now. Portuguese businesspeople themselves had for many years been pressing for entry to be facilitated. This great migration results, therefore, from a great demand for people, to meet immediate needs. And since it is in the genes of the Cape Verdean to emigrate in search of better living conditions, it is legitimate to aspire to a better life, to greater income. Of course if there were in Cabo Verde activities of greater added value, that allowed other incomes to be generated, I am certain that companies would be the first to pay higher salaries. But this mass migration, it is indisputable, constitutes a problem. The bet with the greatest future possibility is for us to manage, here inside, to generate enough economy, enough income, enough companies to allow salaries to be attractive so that it does not pay to emigrate, at least in material terms. The ambition of the country, of society, should be that.

When you speak of better companies, better salaries, what economic reforms could have an impact on companies? That is, if there are any, or else which would be the necessary ones in terms of priority?

It is indisputable that this government adopted another posture in relation to the private sector, with a friendlier environment. There are some reforms under way in a positive direction. There is also a strategic vision for the country, of a platform country that provides services to the outside. If the objectives are realistic and are within our capacities, that vision is correct and could bring more development to the country. What other reforms will help growth? That the state business sector functions better, that it offers services on time and of greater quality. Investments in some infrastructure – God save us from the investments made in the decades of the 2000s, many of them turned into white elephants and are weighing on our public debt. I would say investments in infrastructure, but with a selective perspective: the area of digital services such as, for example, fintechs; the way the State's own services treat foreign direct investment; and continuing to deepen what has been the engine of our development, but from a perspective in which the big hotels increase their linkages with the local economy.

And in terms of challenges, what do you think will be the greatest ones that businesspeople will face in 2025?

Apart from the world's, because about those we know nothing, of the others I would say they are the usual ones: inter-island transport, whether air or maritime. Analysing the passenger data for air transport, counting embarked and disembarked passengers, in international transport, in 2023 we reached 2 million passengers and in that year we managed to recover and surpass the pre-pandemic level of 2019, which was 1.9 million passengers. In 2024, in terms of total passengers, domestic and international, it was possible to reach 3 million passengers, when in 2019 it had been 2.7 million. On domestic air transport, and only in the condition of an external observer and from the news that reaches the public, I would say we lost an opportunity with Binter, which was in the market for a few years. The numbers, to my mind, are sufficiently illuminating. In domestic and international transport, we came from 698,000 passengers carried – when I say passengers I always mean embarked and disembarked, which are usually the figures used – 698,000 in 2015. In 2016, 715,000, all this with TACV. And then in the three years in which Binter is alone in the market and there is no Covid, which is 2017, 2018 and 2019, Binter manages to carry 959,000 in 2017, 884,000 in 2018 and 821,000 in 2019. It is the golden age in terms of domestic passengers. Meanwhile COVID arrives in 2020 and the numbers fall to 249,000, staying at 287,000 in 2021, still in the post-covid recovery and as a result of requirements such as tests for passengers. From 2022, without Binter, which had left the market at the start of 2021, the numbers grow again, reaching 494,000, and grow again in 2023 to 549,000. But with all the problems that the operator acting in the market had, it would have been expected to achieve higher numbers in those years. Part of the demand was certainly left unmet. In 2024, and despite the departure of the previous operator right at the beginning of the year and the entry of TACV only from March 2024 and in a timid way with little supply, it was possible to reach the figure of 612,000 domestic passengers carried, which is already a significant number given that only in the last months of 2024 did TACV have a sufficient number of aircraft to handle demand. Returning to the question of Binter, I as an external observer did not understand the reason for the government not having chosen to take the 30% stake that was foreseen in the agreement with Binter plus the possibility of the government buying 19%. I accept that, in terms of public finances, at that time, and with the serious problems inherited, the government had no appetite to buy and therefore to put more public resources into the sector, even because of the disastrous situation the domestic business was in. The ATR aircraft, which were already more than 70% amortised, had been “sold” to the supplier, then leased back again, losing the “ownership” that had already been held. That was a ruinous option of the administration of the time, sanctioned by the government. Only with the objective of dressing up the accounts. Returning to Binter, the 30% stake for the State, which did not involve the use of public resources, clearly should have been taken. I do not know what happened to lead them to take such a radical attitude of abandoning the market, but from the outset, having made that bet for some years, it is probable that if they had a favourable environment and having proved that it is possible to maintain a viable, efficient and profitable domestic operation in the country, a way could have been found to keep them in the country. I do not know whether they would have had unacceptable demands, but one need only look at the numbers to see that the hole from Covid in 2020 was enormous. And aviation was particularly affected. I usually say that this government works better in emergencies than in what is routine. With more focus and energy. That happened in COVID with the timely and assertive policies and measures that were taken in all areas, but in particular in health and in the economic measures that allowed the country to recover in sanitary and economic terms. And that was achieved in record time. Another example of success of this government, also in an emergency situation, was the solution that was found in a short space of time with the reactivation of TACV in domestic air transport. Of course, with leased aircraft including crew it is a transitional solution because it has unbearable costs and one will have to move towards a definitive solution. We lived through moments of true crisis in the sector, in particular in 2023 when we were at risk of being left without air connections between the islands. A very serious situation. And it was possible to overcome that with a supply that is at this moment stabilised and, from my latest experiences and from what I have heard, working well in general, even in relation to delays and/or cancellations, which will have decreased considerably. And that is a relief for everyone: for businesspeople, for families, even for the tourists who increasingly use the internal connections. In relation to maritime transport, for me, there is an original sin in the tender that was launched: having required five practically new vessels, less than 15 years old, to operate in this market of ours which is so narrow and meagre. We were in the inter-island maritime transport sector between 2003 and 2009, and very sincerely I do not see that the market warranted the need for five vessels, and the investment necessary to have those five vessels less than 15 years old is of such magnitude that there are not enough years to amortise it, that is, it does not allow the recovery of the investment.

Text originally published in the print edition of Expresso das Ilhas no. 1210 of 5 February 2025.

a6916.t:
Muktasari:
- Saa chache baada ya kula kiapo, Rais wa Marekani Donald Trump alisitisha kwa siku 90 misaada ya maendeleo nje ya Marekani, kupisha tathmini ya ufanisi na uwiano na sera yake ya kigeni.
Dar es Salaam. Shirika la Marekani la Maendeleo ya Kimataifa (USAID) limetangaza kusitisha utoaji wa fedha mpya na usambazaji wa fedha chini ya makubaliano ya malengo ya maendeleo (DOAGs) hadi uhakiki wa programu za msaada wa nje zinazofadhiliwa na USAID utakapokamilika.
Wakati mchakato wa kuhakikisha msaada wote wa nje unalingana na ajenda ya sera ya nje ya Rais Donald Trump ukitarajiwa kutolewa ndani ya siku 30, uhakiki huu unatarajiwa kukamilika ndani ya siku 85 kuanzia Januari 24, 2025.
Kutokana na hilo, USAID imewaagiza maofisa wote kusimamisha kazi, mishahara, na safari kwa asasi na taasisi zote zilizopokea misaada kupitia shirika hilo.
Hayo yamebainishwa kupitia barua rasmi kwa maofisa wa mikataba na makubaliano ya USAID na washirika wake, iliyotolewa na shirika hilo Januari 24, 2025.
Barua hiyo, iliyosainiwa na Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa Manunuzi wa USAID, Jami J. Rodgers, imeeleza uamuzi huo unatokana na utekelezaji wa agizo la Rais Trump la kurejelea na kurekebisha misaada ya nje ya Marekani.
“Kulingana na agizo la Rais la kurejelea na kurekebisha msaada wa nje wa Marekani na miongozo ya ziada iliyotolewa na idara ya nchi, USAID inasimamisha utoaji wa fedha mpya na usambazaji wa fedha chini ya makubaliano ya malengo ya maendeleo (DOAGs) hadi uhakiki wa programu za msaada wa nje zinazofadhiliwa na USAID utakapokamilika,” imeeleza barua hiyo.
Kwa mujibu wa Jami, miongozo hiyo inajumuisha msaada wa nje kupitia akaunti zote za programu ("Title III") lakini haitajumuisha gharama za uendeshaji na akaunti ya fedha ya uwekezaji wa msingi ("Title II"). Kuzuia hii kunahusu fedha zinazohusiana na vyombo vyote vinavyopata ufadhili (tuzo).
Amesema kuanzia sasa, maofisa wa mikataba na makubaliano hawataruhusiwa kubadili, kupanua, au kutumia chaguzi au upya wa ufadhili uliopo zaidi ya vitendo vilivyothibitishwa hapa chini.
“Maofisa wa mikataba na makubaliano wanapaswa kutoa maagizo ya kusitisha kazi mara moja, kurekebisha, au kusitisha tuzo zilizopo kulingana na masharti na hali za tuzo husika,” amesema.
Jami amesema baada ya uhakiki, maofisa wa mikataba na makubaliano watawasiliana na watoa huduma na wapokeaji wa tuzo kuhusu maamuzi yatakayofanywa juu ya kama tuzo itaendelea, kubadilishwa, au kusitishwa.
Zaidi ya hayo, maofisa wa mikataba na makubaliano hawataruhusiwa kutoa tuzo mpya au kutoa maombi mapya ya mapendekezo (RFPs), maombi ya maombi (RFAs), taarifa za fursa za ufadhili (NOFOs), au aina yoyote ya ombi la ufadhili wa msaada wa nje hadi kila shughuli itakapohakikiwa na kupitishwa kama inavyowiana na sera ya Rais.
Amesema waziri wa nchi amekubali kutoa maelekezo ya kuzuia kwa mujibu wa agizo la Rais, chini ya uhakiki zaidi, kuhusu maeneo yafuatayo:
“Msaada wa dharura wa chakula na gharama za kiutawala, ikiwa ni pamoja na mishahara inayohitajika kusimamia msaada huo kwa muda; mishahara na gharama za kiutawala zinazohusiana, ikiwa ni pamoja na safari, kwa ajili ya makundi yote ya wakandarasi wa huduma binafsi.
“Gharama halali zilizotumika kabla ya Januari 24, 2025, chini ya tuzo zilizopo, au gharama halali zinazohusiana na maagizo ya kusitisha kazi, kusimamishwa, au marekebisho yanayotokana na kuzuia kutoka katika yale maeneo yanayokubaliwa na Mkurugenzi wa msaada wa nje,” amesema Jami.
Amesema mchakato wa visamaha, pamoja na uhakiki wa shughuli, utatolewa hivi karibuni ndani ya siku 30.
Mkurugenzi wa Idara ya Mpango wa Sera ya Nchi (S/P) au mteule wake atatengeneza viwango vya uhakiki vinavyofaa kuhakikisha msaada wote wa nje unalingana na ajenda ya sera ya nje ya Rais Trump, na unatarajiwa kukamilika ndani ya siku 85 kuanzia Januari 24, 2025.
Januari 20, 2025, saa chache baada ya Trump kuapishwa kwa muhula wake wa pili, alisaini barua ya maagizo akieleza kuwa ni amri ya kiutendaji.
"Viongozi wote wa idara na mashirika yenye jukumu la mipango ya misaada ya maendeleo ya nje ya Marekani wanapaswa mara moja kusitisha majukumu mapya na matumizi ya fedha za misaada ya maendeleo," ilisomeka amri hiyo.
Haikuwa wazi mara moja ni kwa upana gani agizo hilo lililenga, na ni mipango gani, nchi, mashirika yasiyo ya kiserikali, na mashirika ya kimataifa yanayoathiriwa na hatua hiyo
Pia haikufahamika fedha gani zinaweza kukatwa ikizingatiwa kuwa Bunge la Marekani ndilo huweka bajeti ya serikali ya shirikisho la Marekani.
Amri hiyo ya kiutendaji inarudia mtazamo aliokuwa nao Trump wakati wa muhula wake wa kwanza kati ya mwaka 2017 na 2021.
Alipoingia madarakani, alipendekeza kupunguza takriban theluthi moja ya bajeti za diplomasia na misaada ya Marekani, ikiwa ni pamoja na kupunguza kwa kiasi kikubwa ufadhili wa shughuli za ulinzi wa amani za Umoja wa Mataifa na mashirika ya kimataifa. Lakini Bunge la wakati huo lilipinga mapendekezo ya Trump.
a6916.en:
Summary:
- Hours after being sworn in, US President Donald Trump suspended foreign development assistance for 90 days, to allow an assessment of its effectiveness and its consistency with his foreign policy.

Dar es Salaam. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) has announced the suspension of new obligations of funds and the disbursement of funds under development objective agreements (DOAGs) until the review of USAID-funded foreign assistance programmes is completed.

While the process of ensuring that all foreign assistance aligns with President Donald Trump's foreign policy agenda is expected to be issued within 30 days, this review is expected to be completed within 85 days from 24 January 2025.

As a result, USAID has instructed all officers to stop work, salaries and travel for all organisations and institutions that received assistance through the agency.

This was set out in an official letter to USAID contracting and agreement officers and its partners, issued by the agency on 24 January 2025.

The letter, signed by USAID's Chief Acquisition Officer (Executive Director of Procurement), Jami J. Rodgers, explained that the decision stems from the implementation of President Trump's order to review and realign United States foreign assistance.

"Consistent with the President's order to review and realign United States foreign assistance and additional guidance issued by the Department of State, USAID is pausing new obligations of funds and disbursement of funds under development objective agreements (DOAGs) until the review of USAID-funded foreign assistance programmes is completed," the letter stated.

According to Jami, this guidance includes foreign assistance through all programme accounts ("Title III") but will not include operating expenses and the capital investment fund account ("Title II"). This hold applies to funds associated with all entities receiving funding (awards).

He said that from now on, contracting and agreement officers will not be permitted to modify, extend, or exercise options or renewals of existing funding beyond the actions confirmed below.

"Contracting and agreement officers should immediately issue stop-work orders, or modify or terminate existing awards in accordance with the terms and conditions of the relevant award," he said.

Jami said that after the review, contracting and agreement officers will communicate with vendors and award recipients about the decisions that will be made as to whether an award will continue, be modified, or be terminated.

In addition, contracting and agreement officers will not be permitted to issue new awards or issue new requests for proposals (RFPs), requests for applications (RFAs), notices of funding opportunity (NOFOs), or any form of solicitation for foreign assistance funding until each activity has been reviewed and approved as consistent with the President's policy.

He said the Secretary of State has agreed to issue allowances from the hold, pursuant to the President's order and subject to further review, regarding the following areas:

"Emergency food assistance and administrative costs, including salaries necessary to administer that assistance for a period; salaries and associated administrative costs, including travel, for all categories of personal services contractors.

"Legitimate expenses incurred before 24 January 2025 under existing awards, or legitimate expenses associated with stop-work orders, suspensions, or modifications resulting from the hold in those areas approved by the Director of foreign assistance," Jami said.

He said a waiver process, together with the review of activities, will be issued shortly, within 30 days.

The Director of the Office of Policy Planning (S/P) or his designee will develop appropriate review standards to ensure that all foreign assistance aligns with President Trump's foreign policy agenda, and this is expected to be completed within 85 days from 24 January 2025.

On 20 January 2025, hours after Trump was sworn in for his second term, he signed a directive letter stating that it was an executive order.

"All department and agency heads with responsibility for United States foreign development assistance programmes shall immediately pause new obligations and disbursements of development assistance funds," the order read.

It was not immediately clear how broadly the order was aimed, and which programmes, countries, non-governmental organisations and international organisations are affected by the measure.

Nor was it known what funds could be cut, given that the United States Congress is the body that sets the budget of the United States federal government.

That executive order echoes the stance Trump held during his first term between 2017 and 2021.

When he came to power, he proposed cutting roughly one third of United States diplomacy and aid budgets, including sharply reducing funding for United Nations peacekeeping operations and international organisations. But the Congress of that time rejected Trump's proposals.

a7007.t:
La Nation Bénin...
Le président de la République a tenu, samedi 30 mai dernier, une séance de travail avec des responsables en charge du secteur de l’énergie électrique. D'importantes mesures ont été préconisées pour juguler la crise énergétique persistante.
Réuni en séance de travail samedi 30 mai dernier au palais de la République, la Task force sur le secteur de l’énergie a évalué les besoins du pays et étudié les perspectives pour une fourniture optimale de l'énergie à court, moyen et long termes.
Thierno Bocar Tall, Pdg de la Société africaine des biocarburants et énergies renouvelables (SABER) a fait le point des initiatives en matière d'énergies renouvelables et des nouveaux projets envisagés. A l'en croire, la phase 1 du Programme de développement des énergies renouvelables et de l'efficacité énergétique (PRODERE I) a permis de doter le Bénin de centrales solaires, de 1300 lampadaires à basse consommation et des kits solaires. Pour conforter ces acquis, il est mis en œuvre une nouvelle initiative dénommée Programme de valorisation de l'énergie solaire (PROVES). Les financements américain et algérien viendront appuyer ce vaste chantier pour porter à 4000 voire 5000 Kw la capacité du Bénin en matière d'énergies renouvelables, annonce-t-il.
Point de dépliement des compteurs...
De son côté, Claude Gbèdonougbo Gbaguidi, président de l'Autorité de régulation de l'énergie (ARE), a fait le point d'une mission diligentée par le chef de l'Etat au sujet du barrage de Nangbeto momentanément mis aux arrêts en raison des travaux du pont d'Athiémé. Il en ressort que la société SOGEA SATOM en charge des travaux, avec l'appui du génie militaire, s'active pour que d'ici le 15 juin prohain, le pont d'Athiémé en construction ne soit plus un obstacle au bon fonctionnement du barrage  qui injecte dans le patrimoine du Bénin et au Togo une capacité totale de 40 Mw.
Camille Kpogbémabou, directeur général de la Société béninoise d'énergie électrique (SBEE), a quant à lui fait le point du processus de déploiement des compteurs prépayés dans l'administration publique. 85% des structures étatiques sont déjà couvertes par cette opération démarrée en août dernier, confie-t-il, tout en rassurant des mesures correctives prises pour faire face aux exigences de l'opération. Un vaste projet de basculement des 500 000 branchements conventionnels vers le prépaiement est en cours, poursuit-il. 45 000 compteurs prépayés sont déjà disponibles en attendant les 100.000 attendus au titre du Millennium challenge account (MCA). 
Le ministre en charge de l'Energie par intérim Géro Amoussouga, et le Secrétaire général du gouvernement Alassani Tigri rassurent les populations quant aux dispositions prises pour éradiquer et conjurer durablement la crise énergétique au Bénin. 
Dans le court terme, ces mesures envisagées ont trait à la location de groupes électrogènes auprès des sociétés privées, l'approvisionnement en gaz naturel de la centrale de Maria Gléta, la mise en œuvre du nouveau programme national d'énergie rurale, etc. A moyen et long termes, le gouvernement travaille à porter la puissance installée à hauteur de 1500 Mw d'ici fin 2015, avec les 411 millions de dollars du Millennium challenge accourt (Mca), la première phase de 120 Mw dans le cadre de la construction d'une centrale de 400 Mw sous financement de la Banque islamique de développement (Bid), etc.
 
Eclairage public à base du solaire
 
Pour toucher du doigt l'effectivité de certains projets énergétiques, Boni Yayi a fait un tour dans la ville de Cotonou, précisément au quartier Agla. Les lampadaires solaires du Programme de valorisation de l'énergie solaire (PROVES) servent d'éclairage public, au grand bonheur des populations. Selon Félix Comlan Ebo, il s'agit de la première phase avec 650 lampadaires, six mini-centrales. La deuxième phase, financée par les Américains, sera bientôt mise en œuvre pour 1500 lampadaires. 
Au total 15 000 lampadaires seront déployés au titre du projet dont 5000 à Cotonou. D'un montant de 50 milliards Francs CFA, il prend en compte l'électrification des 105 chefs lieux d'arrondissement restants, l'installation de mini-centrales, etc.
a7007.en:
La Nation Benin...

The President of the Republic held, on Saturday 30 May, a working session with officials in charge of the electricity sector. Important measures were recommended to curb the persistent energy crisis.

Meeting in a working session on Saturday 30 May at the Palace of the Republic, the Task Force on the energy sector assessed the country's needs and studied the prospects for an optimal energy supply in the short, medium and long term.

Thierno Bocar Tall, CEO of the African Biofuels and Renewable Energy Company (SABER), gave an update on renewable energy initiatives and the new projects envisaged. According to him, phase 1 of the Programme for the Development of Renewable Energies and Energy Efficiency (PRODERE I) allowed Benin to be equipped with solar power plants, 1,300 low-consumption streetlights and solar kits. To consolidate these gains, a new initiative called the Solar Energy Development Programme (PROVES) is being implemented. American and Algerian financing will support this vast undertaking in order to raise Benin's renewable energy capacity to 4,000 or even 5,000 Kw, he announces.

Update on meter deployment...

For his part, Claude Gbedonougbo Gbaguidi, president of the Energy Regulatory Authority (ARE), gave an update on a mission ordered by the Head of State concerning the Nangbeto dam, temporarily shut down because of the works on the Athieme bridge. It emerges that the company SOGEA SATOM, in charge of the works, with the support of the military engineering corps, is working so that by 15 June the Athieme bridge under construction will no longer be an obstacle to the proper functioning of the dam, which injects a total capacity of 40 Mw into the assets of Benin and Togo.

Camille Kpogbemabou, director general of the Beninese Electricity Company (SBEE), for his part gave an update on the process of deploying prepaid meters in the public administration. 85% of state structures are already covered by this operation, which began last August, he confides, while giving assurances about the corrective measures taken to meet the operation's requirements. A vast project to switch the 500,000 conventional connections over to prepayment is under way, he continues. 45,000 prepaid meters are already available, pending the 100,000 expected under the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA).

The interim Minister in charge of Energy, Gero Amoussouga, and the Secretary General of the government, Alassani Tigri, reassure the population as to the arrangements made to eradicate and durably avert the energy crisis in Benin.

In the short term, these envisaged measures relate to the rental of generators from private companies, the supply of natural gas to the Maria Gleta power plant, the implementation of the new national rural energy programme, etc. In the medium and long term, the government is working to raise installed capacity to 1,500 Mw by the end of 2015 [sic], with the $411 million of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA), the first phase of 120 Mw within the framework of the construction of a 400 Mw power plant financed by the Islamic Development Bank (IDB), etc.

Solar-based public lighting

To see for himself the effectiveness of certain energy projects, Boni Yayi toured the city of Cotonou, specifically the Agla neighbourhood. The solar streetlights of the Solar Energy Development Programme (PROVES) serve as public lighting, to the great delight of the population. According to Felix Comlan Ebo, this is the first phase, with 650 streetlights and six mini power plants. The second phase, financed by the Americans, will soon be implemented for 1,500 streetlights.

In total, 15,000 streetlights will be deployed under the project, of which 5,000 in Cotonou. Worth 50 billion CFA francs, it takes into account the electrification of the remaining 105 district capitals, the installation of mini power plants, etc.

a7040.t:
Genetically modified potato varieties are undergoing field trials and regulatory assessment for massive cultivation in Nigeria.
The varieties, according to experts, are meant to address diseases related to potato farming in the country.
Dr Charles Amadi, Principal Investigator of the Global Biotechnology Potato Partnership (GBPP) made this known in an interactive session with journalists held at the National Institute for policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Jos, Plateau State.
He said, “The partnership aims to conduct field trials and regulatory assessments to ensure the safety and efficacy of the genetically modified potato varieties.
“It works on capacity building and training for farmers, extension workers, and regulators to support the adoption and proper management of these biotechnological innovations.
“The GBPP aims to improve food security by increasing potato yields and reducing crop losses due to diseases and pests.
“It seeks to enhance the livelihoods of smallholder farmers by providing them with more robust and productive potato varieties”
He added that, “We are required by law to do regulatory, national performance and on-farm trials before they can be released. We have to submit dossiers from the regulatory trial to NBMA for consideration for environmental release.
“By eliminating late blight disease, your potato crop yield will be increased and stabilized enabling you to have more food and make more money.
“The late blight-resistant potato is safe and can reduce the cost of growing your potato crop by reducing the need for fungicides by 90%, this leads to less labor costs, stable yields, and better livelihood for your family.
“It reduces the harmful effects of fungicide use on the environment.
“The new variety which had so far gone one year trial is funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) as part of the Feed the Future Global Biotech Potato Partnership.”

a7285.t:
Monday October 13, 2025
Mogadishu (HOL) — The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Somali government have reached a staff-level agreement on the fourth review of Somalia’s Extended Credit Facility (ECF), a deal that could release US$30 million in new funding to support reforms and stabilize the nation’s fragile economy.
The agreement, announced Sunday, follows two weeks of discussions led by IMF Mission Chief Ran Bi and Finance Minister Bihi Egeh in Washington, D.C., and Mogadishu. It will be submitted to the IMF Executive Board for approval in the coming weeks.
advertisements
If approved, the disbursement will bring Somalia’s total ECF funding to nearly US$100 million since the program began in December 2023, as part of a three-year arrangement designed to strengthen fiscal discipline, modernize public institutions, and sustain growth after years of debt relief.Somalia’s economy, which grew 4.1 percent in 2024, is expected to slow to 3 percent in 2025 and 3.3 percent in 2026 due to foreign aid cuts and recurring climate shocks, according to IMF projections. Inflation is forecast to remain stable at 3.5 percent, though food prices are likely to remain high.
Despite these challenges, the IMF noted that Somalia’s fiscal performance has stayed broadly on track. The country’s budget deficit is projected at 0.3 percent of GDP in 2025, rising slightly to 0.75 percent in 2026 as the government expands social spending and prepares for national elections.
Authorities have requested an augmentation of access under the current ECF by SDR 30 million (about US$40 million) to cushion against aid disruptions and fund social programs.
The IMF commended Somalia’s continued reform drive, highlighting strong income tax collection under a new tax law, customs modernization, and strict control over spending.
The Central Bank of Somalia has strengthened its regulatory framework and advanced plans for a future currency board arrangement that would stabilize the Somali shilling. The government has also implemented a new extractive industries law to increase transparency in resource management and attract investment in oil and gas.
“To mitigate the negative impact of foreign aid cuts and support their reform efforts, the authorities have requested an augmentation of access under the ECF arrangement,” said IMF Mission Chief Ran Bi, praising the Somali government’s commitment to reform despite economic challenges.
The ECF program builds on Somalia’s historic debt relief milestone in 2023, when 99 percent of its bilateral debt was cancelled by Paris Club creditors under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative. The move allowed Somalia to regain access to global financial markets for the first time in three decades.
Continued international support, the IMF said, remains crucial to maintain momentum amid uncertainty surrounding aid flows and worsening climate shocks.
If the Executive Board approves the latest review, Somalia will gain access to the next tranche of financing before the end of the year.

a7372.t:
By Spendilove Incoom
The Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Ghana, H.E. Sultan Abdulrahman Al-Dhakel, paid a courtesy visit to the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Hon. Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa (MP), at the Ministry on Tuesday, March 25, 2025.
Discussions centered on strengthening diplomatic ties between Ghana and Saudi Arabia, with a focus on key areas such as the Hajj quota, scholarships, trade, and digitalization. Ambassador Al-Dhakel reaffirmed Saudi Arabia’s commitment to fostering mutually beneficial relations, emphasizing the importance of collaboration for growth and development.
Hon. Ablakwa expressed Ghana’s gratitude for Saudi Arabia’s ongoing support, particularly in education, construction, trade, and humanitarian assistance. He acknowledged Saudi contributions towards aiding inner-city communities and providing relief for victims of recent floods in the Volta Region.
Both parties reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral relations and exploring new avenues for cooperation between the two nations.

…Police Warn #FreeNnamdiKanu Protesters To Obey Court’s Restrictions
…Political Developments Favour Push For IPOB Leader’s Freedom
LAGOS – The Police have warned the #FreeNnamdiKanu Protesters to obey court orders restraining their planned protest on Monday.
In a statement on Saturday, Benjamin Hundeyin, the force spokesperson, warned against the planned protests.
He referred to an order issued by the Federal High Court, Abuja division, on October 17, 2025, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/2202/2025 — Federal Republic of Nigeria v. Omoyele Sowore & 4 others.
He said the order, given by M.G. Umar, restrains the respondents and others acting under their instruction from staging protests within and around Aso Rock, the National Assembly complex, force headquarters, the Court of Appeal, Eagle Square, and Shehu Shagari Way.
Hundeyin was referring to an interim injunction from a Federal High Court in Abuja restraining human rights activist, Omoyele Sowore, and others from organising or participating in the planned protest which seeks to strengthen calls for Kanu’s release.
The order followed an ex parte application filed by the Federal Government through the Nigeria Police, seeking to prevent the planned demonstration in the Federal Capital Territory.
The IPOB leader has been in detention since June 2021 and gone through court trials for alleged terrorism.
In October 2022, the Court of Appeal ordered his immediate release but the Supreme Court, on December 15, 2023, overturned the decision and permitted the Federal Government to continue his trial while he remains in detention.
GROWING AGITATION FOR KANU’S FREEDOM
Concerns over his continued detention and trial have widened in recent times and it is believed that besides the subject of Igbo marginalization, the coming 2027 elections may have drawn political waves around the man that has become a symbol of Igbo agitation for justice within the Nigerian system.
Ambassador Kalu Ofon Emmanuel, Lagos State Chapter President, International Human Rights Protection Service, Naples, Florida, USA, has attributed the recent push for the release of Mazi Nnamdi Kalu, incarcerated leader of the Indigenous Peoples of Biafra (IPOB), to politics.
Dr Emmanuel, who spoke to Sunday Independent, revealed that both the detention and the push for the release of Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, which has been gathering momentum, are all politically motivated.
Recall that several attempts had been made through letters written to both the immediate-past and incumbent presidents of Nigeria to no avail.
Now, as political campaigns are gathering momentum, politicians are warming up for next elections, hence the reason behind the fresh push for Nnamdi Kanu’s release.
Emmanuel cited the recent presidential pardon granted those he termed world-class criminals, terrorists, drug barons, kidnappers, highway armed robbers and killers, who he said should not be seen walking freely on the roads, and wondered why Nnamdi Kanu should not be released from detention.
He maintained that if the judiciary had been reliable, Nnamdi Kanu should have been released long ago, saying that those who derive joy and make merchandise from his detention should think twice as they are not invincible.
Emmanuel indicated that the fresh push for Nnamdi Kanu’s release is due to a rise in political activities for the 2027 general election.
According to him, “The people are holding their voter cards which are their weapons and mandate. If people are not disfranchised and have free and fair elections, the wind will blow soon and their anus will be exposed.”
Rev. Felix Nwosu, while speaking to Sunday Independent, attributed the fresh push for Nnamdi Kanu’s release to the fact that he has been in incarceration for too long, saying that his release is long overdue.
According to him, the fact that President Tinubu did not include Nnamdi Kanu among those granted presidential pardon recently, ignited the fresh push by the Igbo groups and intelligentsia for his release.
Dr Nwosu added that Nnamdi Kanu’s continued incarceration while people who committed heinous crimes are being given presidential pardon has made the call for his release political, which he said will continue to re-echo as the campaigns for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.
He said that Nnamdi Kanu’s continued detention has reopened the cry for marginalisation of Ndigbo since after the civil war, and his release will help to assuage this feeling.
Nwosu stated: “The recent presidential pardon that did not favour Nnamdi Kanu seems to remind Ndigbo that they are not being fairly treated as a people in Nigeria where leaders continue to profess unity, equity and fairness, why not really embracing the Igbo as part of the nation.
“The Nigerian people do not want the marginalisation of Ndigbo anymore. They want equal rights to every Nigerian person. Nigerians feel that Nnamdi Kanu should be among those released for peace to reign in South Eastern Nigeria as his continued detention has caused a lot of chaos in this part of the country.
“If truly we are practising federal character as being prescribed, President Tinubu should look into the case of Nnamdi Kanu for urgent consideration as a gift for Ndigbo.
“Although his case is still pending in court and that those ho bagged presidential pardon are convicts, the president also has the power to instruct the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to discontinue the trial.
AVAILABLE OPTIONS
Also, what is needed is needed now is negotiation and lobbying for him to be granted bail, adding that “Nigerians should not forget Nnamdi Kanu’s suffering as a result of leaving the country when he was granted bail for the first time.”
Nwosu called for serious dialogue between IPOB and the Federal Government, just as was the case in the Middle East between Hamas and the Palestinians and State of Israel for peace to reign in Nigeria more, especially South Eastern Nigeria, which has been in deplorable state, and needs urgent attention.
Also speaking, Hon. Charles Anike, National President, Eastern Union (EU), while speaking on the fresh push for Nnamdi Kanu’s release, said it was due to the realisation that there was no basis or justifiable reason for his continued detention.
According to Hon. Anike, Nnamdi Kanu did not commit any known crime, “except that clueless government of APC under Buhari became too afraid of Kalu’s growing influence and the awareness he was creating among the Igbos.
“That was reinforced by the deep seated hatred of Buhari for the Igbo race. Don’t we really have a constitution? Are there no specified duration for trial of whatever allegations?
“Why the endless court drama? The APC virus has spread and swallowed our judiciary like other institutions, otherwise why would any judge join in the political conspiracies against Nnamdi Kanu who conducted his agitations without violence?”
According to him, Nigerians have seen that whatever crime the Federal Government claimed that Kalu committed, was also committed even more seriously and simultaneously by Sunday Igboho, who has been agitating for Oduduwa Republic.
“So, why should Sunday Igboho not in detention like Nnamdi Kanu, but is walking freely? There are several others in the north who indisputably have been agitating for Arewa State and they were not arrested or detained.
“What about those well-known terrorists that have been on a rampage in the north and have extended their blood thirsty onslaught across the country? If you like, call them whatever names.
“Are they not operating freely and even brandishing their weapons on viral videos? What has the Federal Government done to them?
“Are they not celebrities, to the extent that government officials are publicly and proudly posing in pictures with them in the name of negotiating with them?
“Even those of them (terrorists) that were arrested during ex-President Jonathan’s era were all released by Buhari and many of them, said to be ‘repentans’ allegedly enlisted into the Nigerian Army.
“The reason our military men have become sacrificial lambs to the Boko Haram terrorists. This is the only country in the world where terrorists are celebrated and tolerated. What are we really talking about?
“While hardened terrorists are roaming freely, Nnamdi Kanu will be kept in detention for years for agitating against marginalisation and injustice.
“The fresh push for his release is due to the realisation that Nnamdi Kalu did nothing to warrant his incarceration. Rather his detention is another way of continuing the humiliation of Ndigbo in Nigeria as a people that lost a civil war.
“The recent and renewed effort to free Mazi Nnamdi Kalu from the hostage of APC and its allies from the South-East is a very welcome development. We in the Eastern Union are fully in support and in partnership with the move.
“The time has come for us to stick out our necks for the worst, otherwise these people that have snatched power will continue to take undue advantage of the people to sustain our enslavement.
“This present and renewed effort must be sustained until Nnamdi Kalu is released. Tinubu has no right to sustain Buhari’s illegality.
“Tinubu should take steps to release Mazi Nnamdi Kalu before the date set aside for the protests. He should listen to the people because the voice of the people is the voice of God.”
